full_judgment:
Md. Rezaul Hasan J:- This appeal under Order 43 Rule 1(r) of the Code of Civil Procedure has been preferred by the defendant Appellant against the order No. 10 dated 27.04.2011 passed by Joint District Judgment, 55 Court Dhaka in Title Suit No. 31 of 2011 directing the defendants to maintain status quo for a period of six months and prohibiting from taking any step in respect of the suit cold storage.

2. Facts relevant for the disposal of the appeal are that one Syed Sakhawat Hossain and four others who are respondent Nos. 1-5 in Title suit No. 31 of 2011 against Md. Rezul Karim, Mukta Begum, Md. Khondkar Amirul Islam and Sharif Masudul Hoque as the defendant Nos. l-4 and also impleading Sonali Bank, its Managing Director and two Deputy General Managers as defendant Nos. 5 to 8. The plaintiffs case, in brief, is that they have purchased 100% shares from defendant Nos. 1-3 held by them, in M/S Combined Food Cold Storage Ltd. (a private company limited by shares) certificate of incorporation number C-32902 (20223)/97; that Form 117 were executed by the transferors in favour of plaintiffs and that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 have sworn in affidavit Nos. 85 and 86 on 22.6.07.2006 and defendant No. 3 has sworn in affidavit 17 on 07.08.2006 affirming execution of aforesaid share transfer forms in favour of the plaintiffs. Accordingly the plaintiffs have become 100% owners of the shares in the said company as well as of the landed and other properties, including the cold storage and in the machineries owned by the said company. The plaintiffs also averred that they are in possession of the properties of the said company and that they have deposited Tk. 111.49 lakhs in the Bank, as down payment, to adjust the loan due to the Bank by the said company. Besides, plaintiffs have also entered into a partnership arrangement with defendant No. 4 on condition that the defendant No. 4 would furnish Tk. 3,00,000,00/- (three crores) to enable them to make payment of the Bank loan. Thereafter, the defendants have been trying to change the ownership of the plaintiffs thus acquired by them in the said company and that such an attempt was taken on 20.01.2011. In this situation, the plaintiffs have no other alternatives but to file this suit to protect their title and possession in the suit property as well as to avoid suffering irreparable loss.

3. The plaintiffs have, in the premises, prayed for declaration that the plaintiffs are in exclusive and legal owners of M/S Combined Food and Cold Storage Ltd. as described in the schedule to the plaint as well as they have prayed for some other consequential reliefs stated in the prayer portion, as follows—

“(খ) নিম্নের ‘খ’ তফসিলে বুর্ণিত ৭নং বিবাদীপক্ষ কর্তৃক ১নং বাদীপক্ষের বরাবরে প্রদত্ত বিগত ২৮.২.২০১০ইং তারিখের চিঠি, ৪নং বিবাদীপক্ষ কর্তৃক ১নং বাদীপক্ষের বরাবরে প্রদত্ত বিগত ২২.১২.২০১০ইং চিঠি এবং বিবাদীপক্ষ কর্তৃক ১নং বাদী বরাবরে প্রদত্ত বিগত ২৪.১২.২০১০ইং তারিখের চিঠি অবৈধ, বেআইনি, অকার্যকর ও বাদীপক্ষে উপর বাধ্যকর নহে মর্মে অপর এক ঘোষনামূলক ডিক্রি দিতে।

(গ) নিম্নে ‘ক’ তফসিল বর্ণিত নালিশী মেসার্স কম্বাইন্ড ফুড এন্ড কোন্ড ষ্টোরেজ লিমিটেডতে থাকা বাদীপক্ষের দখল স্থিরতরের ডিক্রি দিতে।

(ঘ) বাদীপক্ষের মালিক দখলীয় নিম্নের ক তফসিল বর্ণিত নালিশী সম্পত্তি মেসার্স কম্বাইন্ড ফুড এন্ড কোন্ড ষ্টোরেজ লিমিটেড হইতে বিবাদীপক্ষগণ যাহাতে জোরপূর্বক ও বেআইনীভাবে বাদীপক্ষকে বা তাহার নিয়োজিত কর্মকর্তা কর্মচারীদেরকে উচ্ছেদ করিয়া বেদখল করিতে না পারে বা উক্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের জন্য ক্ষতিকর কোন কার্যকর করিতে না পারে বা বাদীপক্ষের বৈধ ব্যবসা পরিচালনা করিতে বা উহার সংশ্লিষ্ট যাবতীয় কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করিতে কোন প্রকার বাধা বিঘ্ন সৃষ্টি করিতে না পারে তৎমর্মে বিবাদীগনের বিরুদ্ধে এক চিরস্থায়ী নিষেধাজ্ঞার ডিক্রী দিতে”

4. Alleging the similar facts the plaintiffs also filed a petition under Order XXXIX, Rule 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, with a prayer that the plaintiffs should not be evicted from the suit property of the M/S Combined Food and Cold Storage Ltd, forcefully or illegally etc. At the same time plaintiffs have also prayed for an interim order to that effect.

5. The defendant Ng. 7 Sonali Bank, Corporate branch (although the Sonali Bank and its branch is the same legal entity) submitted a written objection denying all the material allegations and further stating at paragraph No. 28 that—

“২৮। বাদীর মোকাদ্দমা সম্পূর্ণ মিথ্যা, বানোয়াট ও ভিত্তিহীন দাবীর ভিত্তিতে দায়েরকৃত বিধায় বাদীর অস্থায়ী নিষেধাজ্ঞার প্রার্থনা মোতাবেক কোন নিষেধাজ্ঞা প্রার্থনা মেতাবেক কোন নিষেধাজ্ঞা পাইতে পারে না। প্রকৃত ঘটনা নিম্নরুপঃ-

মেসার্স কম্বাইন্ড ফুড কোন্ড ষ্টোরেজ লিমিটেড একটি প্রাইভেট লিমিটেড কোম্পানী যাহার বর্কমান ব্যবস্থাপনা পরিচালক ৩নং বিবাদী খন্দকার আমিনুল ইসলাম টুকু এবং চেয়ারম্যান ১নং বিবাদী মোঃ রেজাউল ইসলাম এবং পরিচালক ২নং বিবাদী মুক্তা বেগম। উক্ত কোম্পানী একটি আধুনীক হিমাগা��� প্রতিষ্ঠার জন্য ৭নং বিবাদী সোনালী ব্যাংকের আর্থিক সহায়তা চাহিলে ব্যাংক গত ১৩.৮.১৯৯৭ইং তারিখে উক্ত কোম্পানীর অনুকূলে ৩,৫৭,৯৮,০০০/- টাকা প্রকল্প ঋণ মনজুর করেন। উক্ত ঋণের জামানত স্বরুপ হিমাগারটি প্রকল্প ভূমিসহ মোট ১.৫৭ একর সম্পত্তি ঋণদাতা সোনালী ব্যাংকের অনুকুলে রেজিঃ মর্টগেজ রাখেন। পরবর্তীতে বিভিন্ন সময়ে কোম্পানীর অনুকূলে বিপুল অংকের চলতি মূলধন ঋণ মনজুর করা হয় যাহা কোম্পানী ভোক করতঃ হিমাগার পেন্ঢজমূলে বন্ধকীকৃত আলু বেআইনি ভাবে বিক্রয় করায় টংগীবাড়ী থানায় গত ২৪.১১.২০০২ইং তারিখে কোম্পানীর পরিচালকগণের বিরুদ্ধে ফৌজদারী মামলা নং-৫/০২ দায়ের করা হয়, যাহা বিচারাধীন আছে। ইহা ছাড়া বিবাদ কোম্পানীর নিকট বকেয়া ঋণের ৮,২১,১৯,৭২০/- (আট কোটি একুশ লক্ষ উনিশ হাজার সাতশত বিশ) টাকা আদায়ের জন্য সোনালী ব্যাংক বাদী হইয়া ১নং অর্থঋণ আদালত, ঢাকায় অর্থঋণ মোঃ নং- ৩১০/২০০৩ দায়ের করে, যাহা গত ২১.৪.২০০৫ইং তারিখে ব্যাংকের অনুকূলে রায় ও ডিক্রী হয়। উক্ত ডিক্রীজারীর নিমিত্তে অর্থজারী মোঃ নং- ৫৭৪/২০০৫ দায়ের করিলে বিজ্ঞ আদালত বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি পর পর দুইবার নিলামে দিয়াও বিক্রয় করিতে ব্যর্থ হইয়া গত ২৭.৪.২০০৯ইং তারিখে অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন ২০০৩ এর ৩৩(৫) ধারায় ভোগ দখল ও বেচাবিক্রির ক্ষমতা যুক্তে বাদী সোনালী ব্যাংকের অনুকূলে এক সনদপত্র ইস্যু করে। উক্ত বন্ধকী সম্পত্তির ভোগ দখলের সনদপত্র মোতাবেক বাদী/ডিক্রীদার সোনালী ব্যাংক বন্ধকী সম্পত্তির ভোগ দখলের ও বেচাবিক্রীর মালিক হিসাবে উহার নিলামে বিত্রয়ের জন্য চেষ্টা করিয়া ব্যর্থ হইয়া পুনরায় কোম্পানীসহ ১-৩নং বিবাদীগণের বিরুদ্ধে ২য় জারী মোকাদ্দমা নং-৯৯/২০১০ দায়ের করেন। যাহাতে গ্রেফতারী পরওয়ানা বর্তমানে ইস্যু হইয়া বিচারাধীন আছেন। চতুর্থ ১নং বিবাদী তাদের বিরুদ্ধে বিচারাধীন মোকাদ্দমা বিদ্যামান থাকা অবস্থায় সম্পূর্ণ বে-আইনী ভাবে নালিশী হিমাগার প্রতিষ্টানটি তাহার দথল/নিয়ন্ত্রণে থাকা কথা থকিলেও যোগসাজসে বাদীগণকে বুঝাইয়া দেয় মর্মে বাদী দাবী করিতেছেন, যাহা ৭নং বিবাদীর নাই বা ছিল না। বাদী ১নং বিবাদীর সাথে যোগসাজশে নালিশী হিমাগারটি অবৈধ ভাবে দখলে চেষ্টা করিতেছে।

6. It thus appears from the record that, M/s Combined Food and Cold Storage Ltd. is a private company limited by shares and that the defendant No. 3 is the Managing Director of the said company, whereas the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are the Directors of the said company. The company thereafter applied to the Sonali Bank Limited on 13 of 1997 for loan of Tk. 3, 57,98,000/- in the form of project loan, to establish a modern cold storage. As security for repayment of the said loan, the loan applicant, i.e. the company represented by its Directors, has offered as collateral security the land of the cold storage ltd. measuring 1.57 acres, by way of executing registered mortgage deed in favour of the Bank. Thereafter the Bank has subsequently has granted working capital loan from time to time in favour of the said company and the working capital loan duly secured by pledging the potatoes stored in the cold storage, owned and established by the company by utilizing the project loan obtained from the Bank But, the Directors committed breach of the terms and conditions of the pledge deed by illegally selling the pledged potatoes without knowledge of the Bank and without depositing the sale proceeds of the pledged goods in the Bank to adjust the loan account and for that reason the Bank had to file a criminal case No. 05 of 2002, which is still pending. Besides, in order to realize outstanding loan of Tk. 8, 21,19,720/- (eight crores twenty one lakh nineteen thousand and seven hundred twenty), the Bank had filed, Artho Rin Suit No. 310 of 2003 in the Artho Rin Court passed judgment and decree in favour of the Bank, on 21.04.2005. On the basis of the said judgment and decree, thus passed in favour of the Bank by the Artho Rin Court, the Bank has started Artho Rin Execution case No. 574/2005, against the judgment debtors, who are the defendant Nos. 1-5 in the Title Suit No. 31 of 2011 and who were the defendants in the aforesaid Artho Rin Suit No. 310 of 2003 the Artho Rin Execution Case No. 574 of 2005, the learned court had put the mortgaged property in auction twice, but it could not be sold. Hence, the decree-holder Bank filed an application under section 33(5) of the Artho Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for issuance of a certificate as per provisions of section 33(5) of the said AM. The executing court accordingly issued a certificate in favour of decree-holder Bank (Sonali Bank) on 27-04-2009 under section 33 (5) of the Ain, that reads as follows:-

“কোন সম্পত্তির” উপ-ধারা (১), (২), (২ক), (২খ), (২গ), (৩) ও (৪) এর বিধান অনুসারে বিক্রয় করা সম্ভব না হইলে, উক্ত সম্পত্তি, ডিক্রিকৃত দাবী পরিপূর্ণভাবে পরিশোধ না হওয়া পর্যন্ত দখল ও ভোগের অধিকারসহ ডিক্রীদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত করা হইবে, এবং ডিক্রিদার উ-ধারা (১), (২), (২ক), (২খ), (২গ), (৩) ও (৪) এর বিধান অনুসারে উক্ত সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় করিয়া অপরিশোধিত ডিক্রীর দাবী আদায় করিতে পারিবে এবং আদালতে ঐ মর্মে একটি সার্টিফিকেট ইস্যু করিবে।”

7. The decree-holder Bank, as such, having received a certificate to occupy and enjoy the mortgaged properties, had tried to sell the mortgaged property through auction, but that also did not fetch positive result. Hence the decree-holder Bank has filed Second Artho Rin Execution Case No. 99 of 2010 against all judgment —debtors, including the company In the Second Execution Case warrant of arrest has been issued and is awaiting execution, but knowing fully well about the judgment and decree of the Artho Rin Adalat and about the pendency of the execution case, the plaintiffs have intentionally suppressed the fact that the suit cold storage was in possession and control of the decree-holder Bank, as per the certificate issued under section 33(5) of the Ain, illegally claimed to have transferred its 100% shares of the debtor-company and also claimed to have taken over the possession of the mortgaged properties that was vested in favour of the Bank by the Artho Rin Adalat, as recorded herein before.

8. Further case, as stated in the written objection, of the Bank is that –

“প্রকৃত পক্ষে সোনালী ব্যাংকের অর্থায়নে প্রতিষ্টিত হিমাগারটি এবং হিমাগারের বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি বন্ধক গ্রহিতা ব্যাংকের বিনা অনুমতিতে দখল বুঝাইয়া দেওয়ার কোন রকম এখতিয়ার ১নং বিবাদীর নাই। বাদীগণ কম্বইড ফুড এন্ড কোল্ড ষ্টোরেজ লিমিটেড এর কোন প্রকার পরিচালক ও শেয়ার হোল্ডার নহেন। তাহার উক্ত কোম্পানীর পরিচালক বা শেয়ার হোল্ডার উহা দেখাইবার মত কোন কাগজ তাদের কাছে নাই বা উক্ত কোম্পানীর তাহার পরিচালক বা শেয়ার হোল্ডার মর্মে কোন কাগজ বা দলীলাদী বিজ্ঞ আদালতে দাখিল করেন নাই। মামলাধীন বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি কোনরকম হস্তান্তরের কোনরুপ আইনগত অধিকার ১-৩ নং বিবাদীগণের সাথে অবৈধ যোগসাজশে একটি রাষ্ট্রায়ত্ত্ব বাণিজ্যিক ব্যাংকের বৈধভাবে অর্জিত বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি হইতে বঞ্চিত করার অসৎ উদ্দেশ্য নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে বেআইনীভাবে প্রবেশ করিয়া নিজেকে উক্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের বৈধ মালিক দাবী করিয়া অত্র মিথ্যা ও বানোয়াট মোকাদ্দমাটি দায়ের করিয়াছেন। প্রকৃতপক্ষে নালিশী হিমাগারটি একটি লাভজনক ব্যবসায় প্রতিষ্ঠিত যাহা অবৈধভাবে আত্মসাৎ করার উদ্দেশ্যে বাদীরা নিজেকে উক্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের মালিকা দাবী করিয়া অত্র মিথ্যা মোকদ্দমা দায়ের করিয়াছেন। অত্র মোকাদ্দমাটি দায়েরের কোন কারণ কস্মিনকালেও সৃষ্টি হয় নাই। ইহা ছাড়া অর্থঋণ আদালত আইনের বিধান মোতাবেক ৩৩(৫) ধারা মোদাবেক ভোগ দখলের সম্পত্তির মালিকানা দাবী করিয়া উক্ত আদালত ব্যতীত অন্য কোন আদালতে উক্ত আইনের ২০ ধারা মোতাবেক অন্য কোন মোকাদ্দমা আইনতঃ ন্যায়তঃ চলিতে পারে না।”

9. The Bank also stated that it has no connection with any letter dated 24.12.2010 which was allegedly issued by defendant No.1 Rezaul Islam, a judgment-debtor in the aforesaid Artho Rin Suit. The Bank has also denied any connection with other letters issued by defendant No. 1 admitting receiving money from the plaintiffs. The Bank has asserted that plaintiffs have acquired no right, title or interest in the properties. Besides, Bank has categorically denied all the allegations, claims and averments made in the petition for temporary injunction.

10. The court below, after hearing the parties, by its order dated 27.04.2011 has passed an order directing the defendants (Bank)to maintain status-quo for a period of six months in respect of the suit properties. Being aggrieved by the said order dated 27.04.2011 the Bank has preferred this Miscellaneous Appeal before this Court.

11. Mr. M. Azizul Haque, learned Senior Advocate along with Mrs. Shamshed Banu, appearing for the appellants mainly submits that a mere perusal of the impugned order clearly shows that the Bank has filed Artho Rin Suit No. 310 of 2003 for realization of outstanding Tk. 3,57,98,000/-and also filed Execution Case No. 574 of 2005 and then a second Artho Rin Execution Case No. 99 of 2011. He next submits that, in the finding of the impugned judgment the court below has recorded that it has not found any reliable documents showing payment of Tk. 1,11,49,000/- as down payment to the Bank, but the court below has then recorded that admittedly the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit cold storage, and also found title of the plaintiffs to the shares of the debtor-company as claimed by the defendant Nos. 1-3, without at all recording whether the plaintiffs has acquired any legal title in the 100% shams in the said company or in any of its properties and that the impugned order is totally perverse and it has been passed in total disregard of the provisions of section 20 and 33(5) of the Artho Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Hence, he has prayed for setting aside the impugned order with exemplary cost against the plaintiffs and the judgment-debtors who have been preventing recovery of the Bank loan outstanding since long, which is public money, by resorting to this harassing and collusive litigation.

12. The learned Advocate Mr. Md. Abdul Malek along with Mr. Md. Ziaur Rahman, appearing on behalf of the respondents 2-5, on the other hand reiterated the similar grounds as are taken in the petitions for injunction. Their particular submission is that there are potatoes of third-party-cultivators stored in the suit cold storage and they are in possession of the said cold storage and unless the order of status-quo is maintained then third party cultivators-would suffer irreparable loss. The learned Advocate has also reiterated that, on 01.01.2007, the defendant No. 1-3 (judgment debtors of the said Artho Rin Suit) have transferred 100% shares in the aforesaid company in favour of plaintiffs-respondents as found by the court below and as has recorded in the impugned order. So the order of status-quo should be maintained and the appeal dismissed. In support of their contention the respondents No. 2-5 relied on the decisions reported in 8 BLD (AD) 29: 40 DLR (AD) 62 submitted at the time of delivering judgment.

13. We have heard the learned Advocates, appearing for both the sides, perused the memo of appeal, including all the materials on record.

14. Facts relevant for the disposal of the appeal have been narrated herein above.

15. Having perused the impugned order, we find that under the title "আলোচনা ও সিদ্ধান্ত", it has been recorded that the defendant No. 1, representing the said company, has established the suit cold storage with the loan obtained from the defendant No. 7 (Sonali Bank Ltd.). The suit cold storage has been mortgaged in favour of the defendant Nor. 7(the Bank). The cold storage was affected by the devastating flood in 1998, there was no power supply and as a result it had to stop its operation. On 20.05.2007 the defendant Nos. 1-3 (of the Title Suit No. 31 of 2001) have adopted a resolution to transfer. their 100% shams and accordingly executed share transfer Form (Form No. 117), duly affirmed by swearing in three affidavits, that the plaintiffs have submitted Form No.117, three affidavits, applications dated 04.03.2010 for power connection, a copy of trade licence, a receipt showing payment of electricity bill, a mutation khatian and a receipt showing payment of Tk. 25 lakhs to the defendant No.7 in the court. The trial court has also recorded that the Bank has filed Artho Rin Suit No. 574 of 2005 for the realization of Tk. 3,57,98,000/- against the said defendant and, after obtaining the judgment and decree in the Artho Rin Suit No. 310 of 2003, the Bank has filed Execution suit No. 574 of 2005 and had tried twice to sell the mortgaged property in auction. But, having failed to do so the Bank has again filed second Execution Case No. 99 of 2010 and that the defendants were trying to collusively hand over the suit cold storage. Thereafter the trial court has found that there was no reliable documents on record to show that the plaintiffs have paid to defendant Nos. 1-3 Tk. 40 lakh to purchase the suit cold storage or that it had made payment of Tk. 1,11,49,000/- to the Bank as down payment. It has further recorded that --

“স্বীকৃত মতে বাদী যেহেতু নাঃ হিমাগারের দখল পরিচালনা করিতেছেন এবং মূল্য প্রদান করুক বা না করুক ১-৩ নং বিবাদী হইতে হিমাগারের সাকূল্য শেয়ার প্রাপ্ত হইয়াছেন। এমতাবস্থায় হিমাগার বন্ধ হইলে বা মালিকানা লইয়া জটিলতা সৃষ্টি হইলে পক্ষগণ ছাড়াও কৃষককূলের অপুরণীয় ক্ষতি হইবে।”

Stating this reason the learned Joint District Judge Mr. Md. Sharif Hossain has passed impugned order directing defendants to maintain status-quo for a period of 6 (six) months. Being aggrieved, this miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the Bank as noted above.

16. As recorded in the impugned order, the defendant Nos. 1-3 (of the Title Suit No. 31 of 2011and judgment debtors in the Artho Rin Suit No. 574 of 2005) had adopted a resolution on 20.05.2007 for transferring their 100% shares in favour of the plaintiffs and these defendants have executed Form 117 in favour of plaintiffs and have sworn in affidavits in support of transfer of shares. The trial court, thereafter, has recorded in the impugned order that the defendant No. 7 (Sonali Bank) has filed Artho Rin Suit No.310 of 2003 in the Artho Rin Court and obtained judgment and decree in that suit for realization of Tk. 3,57,98,000/- Thereafter the Bank has filed two execution cases, respectively numbered as 574 of 2005 and 99 of 2010, the later execution case is still pending before the Artho Rin Court.

17. As such section 27A of the Artho Rin Adalat Ain, 1991 reads as follows;-

Section 27A. "Restrictions on the directors of debtor-Banks -Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no resignation of any director of any debtor shall be effective and no director of any such Bank shall be entitled to transfer or sell his shares without the consent of the Board of Directors of the loan giving Bank or financial institution."

18. Learned Joint District Judge has recorded that before effecting the purported transfer pursuant to the resolution dated 20.05.2007 by the share holders of the debtor company, the company itself was a debtor and a defendant in Artho Rin Suit 310 of 2003 and a judgment debtor of Artho Rin Execution Case No. 574 of 2005. Hence, the question arises as to the validity of transfer of shares by the said three share holder -directors in violation of section 27A of the Bank Companies Act, 1991.

19. Now we find that before and at time of adopting resolution dated 20.05.2007 to transfer 100% shares of the said company by executing Form 117 by the defendant Nos. 1-3 the judgment debtors of the said Artho Rin Suit) the said company was a debtor to the Bank and the Bank has already filed Artho Rin Suit No. 310 of 2003. As such and as per specific and clear provisions 27A of the Bank Companies Act.1991, which is a special law, no transfer of shares was either permitted in law or effective in the eye of law, without the consent of the creditor Bank (the Sonali Bank). In the absence of any materials on record showing that the aforesaid defendant Nos. 1-3 had obtained any consent from the Sonali Bank and that upon such consent entire share of the said company was transferred to the plaintiffs, the plaintiffs had acquired no title, right or interest in the shares of the company or in the cold storage owned and established by the company or in any of its property. As such the court below has totally ignored this specific and special provision of section 27A of the Bank companies Act, 1991 and has passed the impugned order on an absurd reason that —

“স্বীকৃত মতে বাদী যেহেতু নালিশী হিমাগারের দখল পরিচালনা করিতেছেন এবং মূল্য প্রদান করুক বা না করুক সে ১-৩নং বিবাদী হইতে হিমাগারের সমুদয় শেয়ার প্রাপ্ত হইয়াছে।

This finding is not only contrary to the specific provisions of law it is also contrary to the principles of law that no title or interest in any property can be passed without any consideration (except in the case of gift or inheritance). As such, the impugned order is ex facie illegal is liable to be set aside.

20. Besides, it is also a long established principles of law that, an interim order in the nature of status qua or injunction which comes in conflict with any specific provisions of a statute cannot be passed, but the trial court has passed the impugned order which is in conflict with the provisions of section 27A of the Bank companies Act, 1991 and also with section 33(5) and section 20 of the Artho Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and both of them are special statutes.

21. Even the court below has overlooked and ignored the specific bar imposed by section 20 of the Artho Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 attributing finality of the order of the Artho Rin Adalat. Section 20 of the Artho Rin Adalat Ain reads as follows –

“ধারা-২০। অর্থঋণ আদালত আদেশের চূড়ান্ত। এই আইনের বিধান ব্যতিরেকে, কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট ঋণ আদালতে বিচারাধীন কোন কার্যধারা বা উহার কোন আদেশ, রায় বা ডিক্রীর বিষয়ে কোন প্রশ্ন উথ্যাপন করা যাইবে না, এবং এই আইনের বিধানকে উপেক্ষা করিয়া কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট আবেদন করিয়া কোন প্রতিকার দাবী বা প্রর্থনা করা হইলে, ঐরুপ আবেদন কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষ গ্রাহ্য করিবে না।”

22. The trial court has recorded that, the Bank has obtained judgment and decree from the Artho Rin Court, in the Artho Rin Suit No. 310 of 2003. But it has failed to appreciate that no appeal being preferred against the said judgment and decree of the Andre Rin Adalat, the judgment and decree passed by the Artho Rin Adalat has acquired finality and has become conclusive.

<u>23. Besides the trial. Court has also recorded that the Bank has filed Artho Rin Execution Case No. 574 of 2004 for realization of the decrial dues and failed twice to sell the mortgaged property by holding two auctions ( in the execution case) and that the Bank has again filed the second execution case No. 99 of 2010. In that execution case the Artho Rin Adalat has issued a certificate in favour of the Bank under section 35(5) of Artho Rin Adalat Ain, but the Court below has failed to appreciate that the order of the Artho Rin Adalat have become final and conclusive as per section 20 of the Ain.</u>

24. At the some time, the court below has failed to appreciate that it cannot sit as a court appeal over the judgment and decree or orders of Andre Rin Adalats, which have been established under a special statute. Hence, the impugned order is not only illegal, but it raises the ability of this particular Judge to try a case and about his possessing elementary knowledge of laws that are applicable in most of the civil proceedings.

25. When, prima-facie the entire alleged transaction is contrary to the specific provisions of law, namely section 27A of the Bank Companies Act, 1991, section 20 and 35(5) of the Artho Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and section 53D of the Transfer of Property Act,1882, the impugned order cannot sustain. Besides, this kind of order would give indulgence and frustrate the intent of the legislature enacting special law for realization of the loan sanctioned by the banks. Bank relies on the public deposit in allowing credit facilities.

26. Besides, the trial court ought to have found that alleged possession was wholly illegal and the plaintiffs were trespassers in the suit properties and the possession of a trespasser or of any other person instrumental to the trespassers cannot get protection in the manlier as has been given by the court below, who obviously had no jurisdiction to entertain any such application or the suit.

27. Section 53D read as follows, No immoveable property under registered mortgage shall be remortgaged or sold without written consent of the mortgagee, and any re-mortgage or sale made otherwise shall be void. Now having noted in the impugned order that –

“মিলটি ৭নং বিবাদী বরাবর মর্টগেজ দেওয়া আছে।” how the court below could proceed upon to pass the impugned order?

28, The court below failed to consider the balance of convenience or inconvenience in this case, while it has totally ignored the fact that the decree holder Bank holding a certificate under section 33(5) of the Ain, will suffer irreparable loss, if such an order is passed. It has put the Bank into jeopardy by passing the impugned order and thereby frustrating in Artho Rin Execution process to be disposed of within a bounded time.

29. We have found no written, objection was filed by defendant Nos. 1-3 who are alleged to have executed share transfer Form and the situation also supports the argument of the appellant that these defendant Nos. 1-3 are acting in collusion with the plaintiffs.

30. The decision reported in 8 BLD (AD) 29: 40 DLR (AD) 62 Mozhar Sowdagor vs M. Zahirul Islam has no manner of application in this case as because the said decision, is regarding a suit filed by a bidder along with prayer for temporary injunction to restrain, the defendants (Bangladesh Shipping Corporation and others) from selling the vessel to anybody else. The apex court, in that case, has held that, a tender making highest offer cannot acquire any right to purchase the vessel. That case has no manner of application in the case before us.

31. We find merit in the Rule, as well as in the submissions that the appeal should be allowed with exemplary cost against respondents.

In the result, the appeal is allowed with cost of Tk. 50,000/00 to be paid within 15 (fifteen) days of the order being received in Court below. The plaintiffs respondents, shall make payment of the cost directly to the concerned branch and shall submit receipt thereof in the court below. The impugned order No. 10 dated 27.04.2010, passed by learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 31 of 2011 is hereby setaside. Let a copy of this judgment and order be sent the Secretary, Ministry of law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs for their evaluation of the judicial functions of the learned Judge Mr. Mohammad Sharif Hossain Hayden and another copy of the judgment be sent to the controlling officer to see if similar orders were passed in any other cases and to evaluate the overall performance as a judicial officer. Let another copy of the judgment be sent to the learned Registrar, Supreme Court for record. The trial court is directed to dispose the suit as expeditiously as possible, preferably within 60 (sixty) working days of receiving the judgment and order of this Division.

Communicate the order at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal, J: By this Rule the opposite parties were called upon to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 27.01.2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Nawabgonj in Title Appeal No.118 of 1998 reversing those dated 26.10.1998 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Gomestapur, Nawabgonj in Other Class Suit No. 38 of 1987 decreeing the suit should not be set aside.

2. The brief facts relevant for disposal of this Rule are that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No.38 of 1987 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Gomestapur, Nawabgonj for declaration that the Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds dated 13.01.1974 allegedly given by the predecessor of the plaintiffs in favour of the defendant Nos. 1-6 are forged, collusive, illegal and created by false personification and as such the same are in effective and not binding upon the plaintiffs and also for partition of the property as given in 'Ka', `Kha' and `Ga' schedule of the plaint stating, inter-alia, that the suit land as given in schedule 'Ka', 'kha' and `Ga' of the plaint was originally belonged to Bilat Ali Mondal, the predecessor of the plaintiffs and defendants; that Bilat Ali Mondal married seven times, who died leaving behind his last wife Fakimon Bibi, the mother of the plaintiffs; that before his death he transferred some properties measuring 1.32 acres of land on 12.01.1961 in favour of the mother of the plaintiffs in lieu of her dower besides this he did not transfer any land to any body; that the defendants claimed the land transferred to them by two Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds and thereupon, the plaintiffs inquired into the matter and came to learn that the said two forged Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds were created after the death of their father Bilat Ali Mondal by false personification. Hence the suit.....

3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying the case of the plaintiffs stating, inter-alia, that the suit of the plaintiffs is not maintainable inasmuch as there was no cause of action to institute the suit; that the suit is barred by limitation and bad for defect of parties; that the defendants case is that the suit land was originally belonged to Bilat Ali Mondal, who transferred the suit land to defendant Nos. 1-6 by executing two Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds; that the alleged deed dated 12.01.1961 in favour of the mother of the plaintiffs are false, forged and fabricated and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. Upon the pleadings of the parties the trial Judge framed 4 issues to decide the suit. At the trial the plaintiffs examined 6 PWs. and the defendants examined 7 DWs. and both the parties proved number of documents in support of their respective cases.

5. The learned Assistant Judge, Gomestapur, Nawabgonj on consideration of the materials on record by his judgment and decree dated 26.10.1998 decreed the suit on contest as prayed for.

6. Being aggrieved thereby, the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No.118 of 1998 before the District Judge, Nawabgonj which was ultimately heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st  Court, Nawabgonj, who by his judgment and decree dated 27.01.2000 allowed the appeal and set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Against which the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners obtained the present Rule.

7. Mr. Abul Quasem, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioners in the course of argument after placing the judgments of two Courts below and other material evidences including the exhibits submits that the plaintiff-petitioners having been succeeded to prove that Haji Bilat Ali, father of the plaintiff-petitioners transferred 1.32 acres of land to Faki Bibi, mother of the plaintiff-petitioners by a registered deed of kabala dated 11.2.61 in lieu of her dower money as well as the defendant opposite parties created two false deeds of Heba-bil-Ewaz being deed No.7545 dated 28.3.74 and 7547 dated 28.3.74 after the death of Haji Bilat Ali Mondal by false personification in which 1.32 acres of land previously given to Faki Bibi by registered deed No.1313 dated 11.2.61 (Ext. No.3) has also been included along with entire property left by Haji Bilat Ali but the Court of appeal below acted illegally in allowing the appeal and dismissing the suit without reversing the finding of the trial Court regarding genuineness of the Heba-Bil-Ewan deeds being Deeds No.7546 and 7547 dated 28.3.1974. Mr. Quasem, referring to the death certificate (Ext.4) of Haji Bilat Ali Mondal emphatically submits that the death certificate of Bilat Ali Mondal (Ext.4) issued by the UP Chairman as per office report of sanitary inspector which being a public document but the Court of appeal below acted illegally in discarding the same. More so, it is evident from the record that the defendant No.1 in his cross-examination did not or could not say the date of death of Haji Bilat Ali Mondal.

8. Mr. Abul Quasem then submits that the defendants did not produce original Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds being Deeds No.7546 and 7547 dated 28.3.1974 in the Court and they did not take any step to prove those deeds as genuine by comparing the signature of thumb impression therein by hand writing expert. The learned Advocate further submits that the suit land is situated in the jurisdiction of Gomostapur Sub-Registry Office but the two deeds of Heba-Bil-Ewaz under challenge were registered in the Nawabgonj Sub-Registry Office having no jurisdiction which is far away from the Gomestapur Sub-Registry Office but the lower appellate Court having lost sight of section 28 (2) of the Registration Act allowed the appeal considering the fictitious documents of the defendant No. 1 as genuine.

9. Mr. Abul Quasem made another plank of attract in the impugned judgment by submitting that the lower appellate Court being misdirected has come to a finding at his own motion that it is not believable after the death of Bilat Ali Mondal his sons (defendants) created two registered deeds of Heba-Bil- Ewaz in the name of their deceased father by way of false personification inspite of sufficient evidence both oral and documentary on record that Haji Bilat All died on 7.02.1974 and the impugned deeds were fraudulently created on 28.3.1974 in the name of Haji Bilat Ali by way of false personification and as such the impugned judgment of the Court of appeal below is liable to be set aside. Mr. Abul Quasem finally submits the findings arrived by the trial Court below have been rested upon consideration and discussion of legal evidences and materials on record and also on a correct and proper analysis of the legal aspects involved in the suit and as such the same should he restored by this Court in the exercise of power under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

10. Mr. Abul Quasem, in support of his submission has relied on the decisions reported in 5 BLC(AD) 76, 10 MLR(AD) 200, 54 DLR 354 and 49 DLR(AD) 151.

11. On the other hand, Mr. Mozammel Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-opposite parties by filing counter affidavit opposes the Rule. He submits that the impugned judgment and decree which was, according to him just, correct and proper. He submits that the impugned judgment is a proper judgment of reversal inasmuch as the lower appellate Court after properly adverting to the evidence on record and to the findings of the trial Court correctly arrived at a finding that Haji Bilat Ali Mondal executed the disputed deeds and the plaintiff failed to prove their case that the deeds are forged. Mr. Mozammel, further submits that the judgment of the trial Court below is shockingly perverse and illegal inasmuch as the said court determined issue No.1 on maintainability of the suit against the established principles of law that all the ejmali properties are to be brought into the Hotch potch of the suit which was correctly noticed by the Appellate Court and in doing so the trial Court did not consider S. A. khatians No.400 and 108 vide Ext. A and A(1) by which the plaintiffs were given earlier 5.23 acres of land by Haji Bilat Ali Mondal but those lands were not brought into the Hotch Potch of the suit. Mr. Mozammel further argues that the originals of the alleged death certificates, which are substantive evidence were not called for, so the certificates of the U.P. Chairman or of the sanitary inspector can not be accepted, when those certificates are against the registered deeds.

12. Referring to the evidence of DWs. Mr. Mozammel submits that another serious error of law, occasionally failure of justice is that the learned trial court did not at all consider the evidence on possession by the defendants although, the D.W.1 was adequately corroborated by D.W.4-7 on the question of possession over the suit land. Apart from that, defendant No. 1 exhibited 4 rent receipts namely Ext. Nos. 6, 6(1)-6(3), which also manifests the possession of the defendants in the suit land and such possession of the defendants demonstrates in the suit land that the questioned deeds have been acted upon. The learned Advocate then submits that the questioned deeds were registered in Chapainawabganj Sub-Registry Office is not an illegality, nor the deeds contain any property over which the executant has no title or any fictitious land has been included therein and as such these deeds are legal and genuine. Mr. Mozammel, finally submits that the findings arrived at by the lower appellate Court have been rested upon consideration and discussion of legal evidences and materials on record and also on a correct and proper analysis of the legal aspects involved in the suit and as such the impugned judgment should not be disturbed.

13. Mr. Mozammel Haque, to fortify his submission has relied on the decisions reported in 19 BLD(AD) 240, 2 MLR(AD) 16, 52 DLR 491, 39 DLR(AD) 223, 35 DLR 132, 22 BLD(AD) 117, 35 DLR(AD) 211, 4 BLC(AD) 191, 8 BLC(AD) 67, 9 BLC 624, 17 BLD(AD) 294 and PLD 1958(SC) 115.

14. These are the points which were argued by the learned Advocates for the respective parties. Now to deal with the contentions raised by the parties it would be convenient for me to decide first of all the question of genuineness of the Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds being Deeds No.7546 and 7547 dated 28.3.1974. It appears that PW-1 Md. Mansur Ali, stated in his deposition that his father Bilat Ali Mondal died on 7.02.1974 and thereafter, his step-brothers namely defendant Nos. 1-3 by way of false personification created two deeds of Heba-Bil-Ewaz being Deeds No.7546 and 7547 dated 28.3.1974 in the name of their deceased father in order to grab their deceased father's entire property including 1.32 acres of land previously given to Fakimon Nessa by registered deed No.1313 dated 11.2.61 (Ext. No.3). PW-3, Latifur Rahman as Sanitary Inspector of Gomestapur Police Station stated that as per death register Haji Bilat Ali Mondal died on 7.02.1974. PW-4, Tajuddin Ahmed is deed writer, who stated that: " আমি দলিল লেখক। বাদী বিবাদীকে চিনি। তার পিতা হাজী বিলাত আলী দফাদার। ফাকিমন বিবিকে চিনি। ও দলিল লিখেছি। গ্রহীতা ফাকিমন, দাতা হাজী বিলাত আলী আমার সম্মুখে টিপ সহি দিয়েছে। এই সে দলিল(একজিবিট-৩)" PW- Zakaria Munna, stated in his deposition that: " বিলাত আলীর স্ত্রী ফাকি বিবিকে চিনতাম। তার বাড়ীর পাশেই আমার বাড়ী। বিলাত আলীর বাড়ীর পাশই আমার বাড়ী। বিলাত আলী ফাকি বিবিকে রামচন্দ্রপুর মৌজায় ১.৩২ একর(৪ বিঘা) জমি তার মোহর বাবদ ৩৭ বছর আগে প্রদান করে। এই জমি ফাকি বিবির ছেলেরা দখল করে। বিলাত আলী মারা গেছেন। বিলাত আলী ২৪ বছর আগে মাঘ মাসে মারা গেছে। এই জমি বাদে বিলাত আলীর অন্যান্য জমি বাদী বিবাদীরা খায়।’’ PW-6, Sultan stated in his deposition that before 24/25 years ago Haji Bilat Ali gifted four bighas land to Faki Bibi as dower money. This witness also stated that: "এই জমির পাশে আমার জমি আছে। এই জমি বাদীরা খায়।

15. The above quoted evidence shows that Haji Bilat Ali Mondal died on 7.02.1974, who during his life time transferred 1.32 acres of land on 12.01.1961 in favour of his wife Faki Bibi (mother of the plaintiffs) in lieu of her dower.

16. Now, let me examine the relevant evidence of DWs. with regard to the question of genuineness of the Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds being Deeds No.7546 and 7547 dated 28.3.1974. It appears that defendant No. 1. Md. Sher Mohammad himself was examined as DW-1, who stated in his deposition that on 28.3.1974 their father Haji Bilat Ali by executing two Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds gifted the suit land in favour of them. This witness proved the Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds dated 28.3.1974 as Ext. 'A' and `A-11. This witness in cross-examination stated that: "আমার পিতা কোন তারিখে মারা গেছে আমার স্মরন নাই " This witness denied the suggestion that on 7.02.1974 his father Haji Bilat Ali died. This witness in cross-examination denied that they fraudulently created Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds dated 28.3.1974 after the death of their father Haji Bilat Ali by false personification. DW-2, Abdul Karim- and DW-3, Abdus Salam both of them in their respective evidence proved the impugned deeds dated 28.3.1974 and DW-3, identified Haji Bilat Ali. It also appears that DW-4, DW-5, DW-6 and DW-7 deposed nothing with regard to the genuineness of Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds being Deeds No.7546 and 7547 dated 28.3.1974.

17. On assessment of the evidence of DWs. it appears that DW-1 in order to prove the actual date of death of their deceased father Haji Bilat Ali could not produce any death certificate rather this witness in his cross examination stated that he could not recollect the date of death of his father Haji Bilat Ali. It also appears that all the D.Ws are close relation of the defendants, D.W. 3 Abdus Salam, who admitted that he is the full brother of the wife of defendant No.3 Fazlur Rahman.

18. Mr. Abul Quasem submits that the defendant opposite parties did not produce original Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds being deeds No.7546 and 7547 in the court and they filed certified copies of their deeds dated 28.3.1974 for which the plaintiff-petitioners could not pray for comparing the thumb impression of those deeds by thumb expert.

19. It is found that PW-1, in his evidence categorically stated that his father Haji Bilat Ali died on 7.02.1974 and his step brothers namely defendant Nos. 1-3 after the death of their father in order to grab their father's property created two forged Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds on 28.3.1974 in the name of his deceased father by false personification. It is also found that the Sanitary Inspector, Latifur Rahman was examined as PW-3, who as official witness proved the death certificate of Haji Bilat Ali.

20. Mr. Abul Quasem, drawing my attention to the evidences adduced by the DWs. and written statements of the defendants submits that it is the case of defendants that their father Hazi Bilat Ali transferred the suit property by two deeds of Heba bil ewaz with the satisfaction of their care but fact remains that they could not able to say the date of death of their father Haji Bilat Ali which clearly indicates that those Heba-bil-ewaz deeds were created fraudulently on 28.3.74 after the death of Haji Bilat Ali by false personification only to grab the suit property.

21. It is found that defendant-opposite parties raised a point regarding maintainability of the partition suit without making all concern co-sharers as parties and without bringing the entire properties of the deceased owner of Hazi Bilat Ali in common hotch potch but they could not specifically give the name of the persons not made parties in the suit and again regarding common hotch potch of partition suit they could not mention any property left by the deceased owner which was left out from the schedule of the suit. In the case of Safaruddin and others Vs. Fazlul Huq and others reported in 49 DLR(AD) 151, where it has been laid down that no suit can fail by reason merely of non-joinder of parties. Order 1 Rule 9 CPC makes this legal position clear. Therefore, I find no merit in the submission of the learned Advocate for the opposite parties.

22. On a careful consideration of the entire evidence on record vis-a-vis the death certificate (Ext.4), I find no possible reason to differ with the view taken by trial Court that: "বাদী প্রমাণ করিতে সক্ষম হইয়াছেন যে, বিলাত আলী মন্ডল গত ইং ৭/২/৭৪ তারিখে মারা গিয়াছেন। বিলাত আলী মন্ডল উক্ত তারিখে মারা যাওয়ায় তাহার পক্ষে বিবাদীপক্ষ বরাবর নালিশী ৭৫৪৬ ও ৭৫৪৭ নং হেবাবিল এওয়াজ দলিল ২টি মৃত ব্যক্তি হসিবে ২৮/৩/৭৪ তারিখে রেজিষ্ট্রী করিয়া দিতে পারেন না।”

23. It is found that the Court of appeal below in deciding the question with regard to the genuineness of Heba-Bil-Ewaz deeds observed that: " অপর লোককে পিতা বানাইয়া দলিল রেজিষ্ট্রী করা হয়। ইহা সম্ভবপর নহে বলিয়া আমি মনে করি।” "

24. On an analysis of the evidence on record, it appears to me that the above observation of the Court of appeal below is not only being based upon gross misreading of evidence on record also being based on misinterpretation of material evidences on record. I, therefore, find that there is a good deal of substance in the contentions raised by Mr. Abul Quasem and the view taken by the appellate Court below cannot be legally sustained.

25. There is another aspect of this case. It is found the suit land is situated within the jurisdiction of Gomostapur sub-Registry Office but the two deeds of Heba-bil-ewaz under challenge were registered in the Nawabganj Sub-Registry Office having no jurisdiction which is far away from the Gomostapur sub-registry Office which also creates serious doubt upon the genuineness of the impugned deeds.

26. In this connection section 28(2)(b) of the Registration Act (XVI of 1908) reads as follows:-

(b) "a document the registration of which is secured by the inclusion of a non-existent, fictitious or insignificant portion or item shall not in any manner affect the rights of a person who was not a party thereto and acquired rights in the property without notice of transaction to which such document related."

27. So, in my view the lower appellate Court on this point also without applying its judicial mind at all to the relevant legal provision allowed the appeal considering the fictitious documents of the defendant No.1 as a genuine.

28. Mr. Mozammel, the learned Advocate at the end of the day submits that the trial Court did not at all consider the evidence on possession by the defendants.

29. In reply, Mr. Abul Quasem, drawing my attention to the evidences adduced by the PWs and DWs and then submits that PW-1, PW-5 and PW-6 categorically testified that Haji Bilat Ali transferred 1.32 acres of land to Faki Bibi, mother of the plaintiff-petitioners by a registered deed of kabala dated 11.2.61 in lieu of her dower money and the plaintiff-petitioners have been owing and possessing the same.

30. On consideration of the materials adduced by the parties, I find sufficient reasons to hold that Fakimon Nessa, the mother of the plaintiff-petitioners having been put into possession over 1.32 acres of land by Haji Bilat Ali in the strength of kabala dated 11.2.61. Therefore, the last contention of Mr. Mozammel, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties is of no substance.

31. The decisions cited by the learned Advocate Mr. Mozammel for the opposite parties have no manner of the application in this case inasmuch as facts of those cases are quite distinguishable from the facts of the present case.

<u>32. Having given my best consideration to the materials on record both oral and documentary, I hold that the impugned judgment and decree of the appellate Court below suffers from illegalities in many folds, it cannot be sustained in law and is liable to be set aside and the findings arrived at by the trial Court below have been rested upon consideration and discussion of legal evidences and materials on record and also on a correct and proper analysis of the legal aspects involved in the suit.</u>

33. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and decree dated 27.01.2000 passed by the Sub-Judge, 1st Court, Nawabgonj in Title Appeal No. 118 of 1998 is set aside and the judgment and decree dated 26.10.1998 passed by the Assistant Judge, Gomestapur, Nawabgonj in Other Class Suit No.38 of 1987 is hereby restored.

34. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

35. Let a copy of this judgment along with lower Courts record be sent down at once.

End.

lawyer:
Mr. M. Khaled Ahmed, Advocate ------ For the appellant. 
Mr. Md. Quamrul Haqie Siddique with Mr. Ahmed Nowshed Jamil, Advocates ------ For the respondent No.6.
parties:
Bangladesh Krishi Bank.
Vs.
M/s. Dadajee Ice Plant and Cold Storage Ltd. And others
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal, J.- This appeal at the instance of the plaintiff-appellant, Bangladesh Krishi Bank represented by the Manager, Bangladesh Krishi Bank, Laban Chara (Rupsha West), Branch-1, Rupsha, Approach Road, Khulna is directed against the judgment and decree dated 25.5.2004 (decree signed on 01.6.2004) passed by the learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna in Artha Rin Suit No.103 of 2001.

2. The brief facts of the case are that the appellant as plaintiff- Bank instituted Artha Rin Suit No.103 of 2001 before the Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna impleading the respondent-defendants for recovery of its outstanding dues amounting to Tk.1,21,02,510.00 as on 11.11.2001 on the averments that in terms of Asian Development Bank loan No. 329 Bangladesh Krishi Bank was entrusted to establish three Ice Plants in Bangladesh and in terms thereof the defendant-respondents decided to establish Ice Plant and cold storage on the supply of the necessary machineries on payment of fund in foreign currency and the defendant would purchase land and construct Factory building for establishment of the Ice Plant and Cold Storage and thereupon, an agreement was executed on 15.6.1985 between the concerned parties and the plaintiff bank granted a loan sanction letter on condition that the Krishi Bank would supply the machineries on payment of fund in foreign currency and the plaintiff would purchase land and construct Factory building for establishment of the Ice Plant and Cold Storage. It was agreed upon that the loan would be sanctioned in foreign currency and not in Bangladesh, Currency. A tripartite contract was entered into between M/s Jain Enterprise on 16.5.1985 for supply of machineries and other materials and in the said contract Frick Company of U.S. represented by its local Agent Messers Eastern Trading Agency Ltd. was the first party and in the 2nd agreement Covington Diseal of U. S. A represented by local Agent Messers Eastern Trading Company was the first party and in both the agreements 2nd and 3rd parties were respectively plaintiff-Bank and the defendant company. The defendant company in terms of the agreement deposited 10% of L/C margin with Bangladesh Krishi Bank, Labonchora Branch and also opened L/C on 18.6.1985 in the Principal Office of Janata Bank, Dilkusha Commercial Area and thereafter, the plaintiff-Bank as per terms and conditions of the agreements time to time supplied the machineries to the defendant-company but defendant company failed to perform his part of the contract and also could not go into operation of its project. In such circumstances plaintiff-Bank under the legal compulsion issued so many money call back notices upon the defendant-company lastly, on 24.7.1995 but the defendant-company having done nothing and hence the suit.

3. The defendant-company contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint contending inter-alia that as per terms and conditions of the agreements the plaintiff-Bank could not or did not supply the entire machineries including Air Blower and Amonia Gas without which the project in question cannot go in operation and the defendant-company did not receive any farthing/ cash money from the plaintiff-Bank as loan. It has been further contended that for non-performance of contract the defendant-company as plaintiff earlier filed a suit being Title Suit No. 26 of 1992 before the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna against the plaintiff-Bank praying for a decree for declaration that the deed of agreements between the parties be cancelled and for recovery of compensation to the tune of Tk. 25 Lac and the said suit was decreed on contest and as such the suit is barred by law of res-judicata.

4. At the trial plaintiff examined 1 witness namely PW-1 and the defendant-company also examined 1 witness namely DW-1 and both the parties also filed documentary evidences to prove their respective cases.

5. The Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna upon hearing the parties and on considering the materials on record dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 25.5.2004 (decree signed on 01.6.2004) mainly on three counts that; firstly, the plaintiff-Bank by adducing evidence could not prove that as per terms and conditions of the contracts the machineries were properly supplied to the defendant company by the plaintiff bank for establishment of the Ice Plant and Cold Storage and due to fault of the defendant-company the Ice Plant and Cold Storage but could not be established and any cash money was sanctioned as loan to the defendant company, secondly, the plaintiff-Bank on the basis of agreement Nos. 152 and 153 filed the suit against the defendant-company for recovery of its outstanding dues with interest but the said agreements have already been cancelled by judgment and decree dated 3.9.1995 passed by the Subordinate Judge,1st Court Khulna decreeing Title Suit No.26 of 1992 and said the judgment and decree was affirmed by the High Court Division in F.A. No.29 of 1996, thirdly, the suit was barred by law of limitation in view of the provisions of section 46 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003.

6. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree the plaintiff-Bank as appellant preferred the instant First Appeal before this Court.

7. Mr. M. Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant in the course of argument has taken us through the impugned order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, deposition of witnesses namely, PW-1 and DW-1 and other materials on record and then submits that Bangladesh Krishi Bank as financial institution executed total 5 agreements time to time with the defendant-company and thereunder sanctioned loan in favour of the defendant company to establish Ice Plant and Cold Storage although the defendant-company could not or did not go into operation of its Ice Plant and Cold Storage but the Artha Rin Adalat giving a go-by to such material aspects of the case mechanically dismissed the suit on the ground that the plaintiff-Bank could not prove its case.

8. Mr. Khaled, next upon referring a bundle of Exhibits submits that all these agreements demonstrate that the plaintiff-Bank as per terms and conditions of the agreement sanctioned loan in favour of the project of defendant-company and as such the Artha Rin Adalat ought to have decreed the suit as prayed for. Mr. Khaled, finally referring to the impugned judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.26 of 1992 submits that the subject-matter of this suit is completely distinguishable from the subject-matter of that suit inasmuch as the present suit was filed by the financial institution for recovery of its loan under Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 and earlier Title Suit No.26 of 1992 was filed by the defendant-company praying for decree for a declaration that the deed of agreements between the parties be cancelled and for realisation of compensation to the tune of Tk. 25 Lac against the Bank and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside.

9. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Quamrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-respondent No.6 supports the impugned judgment and decree dated 25.5.2004 (decree signed on 01.6.2004) passed by the Artha Rin Adalat which was, according to him just, correct and proper. Mr. Quamrul Haque, next after placing the deposition of PW-1 and the plaint of the suit submits that there is nothing on record to show that the plaintiff-Bank at any point of time sanctioned any cash money as loan in favour of the defendant-respondent-company.

10. Drawing our attention to the terms and conditions of the agreements the learned Advocate further submits that it was the duty of the plaintiff-Bank to supply all the machineries to the defendant-company on payment of fund in foreign currency but the plaintiff-Bank miserably failed to do so, as a result of which the Ice Plant and Cold Storage of the defendant-respondent could not go on production. The learned Advocate further submits that the present defendant-respondent earlier as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.26 of 1992 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Khulna praying for a decree declaring the deed of agreement between the parties be cancelled and for recovery of compensation to the tune of Tk. 25,00,000/- and the said suit was decreed on contest wherein the trial Court observed that defendant-bank (petitioner) is guilty for non-performance of his part of the contract resulting in causing huge loss to the plaintiff (respondent). Mr. Quamrul Haque Siddique, finally submits with force that the Bangladesh Krishi Bank as plaintiff deliberately after long tapes of 10 (ten) years instituted the present suit against the defendant-company before the Artha Rin Adalat for recovery of its loan amounting to Tk. 1,21,02,510.00 with interest and it is on record that the loan was sanctioned on the basis of three agreements/ contracts namely agreement Nos. 123, 124 and 125 and the said agreements have been cancelled in Title Suit No.29 of 1992 long before filing the suit and the same was affirmed up to the Appellate Division in F.A. No.29 of 1996 and C.P.L.A: No.191 of 2004 respectively and as such the trial Court bellow rightly dismissed the suit on assigning sound reason.

11. These are the points which were argued by the learned Advocates for the respective parties, now to deal with the contentions raised by the parties before us it would be convenient for us to decide first whether the Artha Rin Adalat was right in holding that the plaintiff bank could not prove its case and thus, the plaintiff bank is not entitled to get a decree as prayed for. It appears that in terms of Asian Development Bank loan No.329 Bangladesh Krishi Bank-was entrusted to establish three Ice Plants in Bangladesh and in terms thereof the defendant-respondents decided to establish Ice Plant and cold storage on the supply of the necessary machineries on payment of fund in foreign currency and the plaintiff would purchase land and construct Factory building for establishment of the Ice Plant and Cold Storage and thereupon an agreement was executed on 15.6.1985 between the concerned parties and the plaintiff bank granted a loan sanction letter on condition that the Krishi Bank would supply the machineries on payment of fund in foreign currency and the plaintiff would purchase land and construct Factory building for establishment of the Ice Plant and Cold Storage.

12. In order to resolve the point whether the Artha Rin Adalat was right in holding that the plaintiff bank could not prove its case a portion of the terms and conditions of agreements (Ext.2) & (Ext. 18) are required to be referred to for having a better view of the dispute in question.

A portion of the Ext.2 reads as follows:

(a) Foreign currency Loan will be disbursed under ADB Credit No.329 BAN (SF) by way of opening a confirmed irrevocable letter of Credit through the designated Bank for import of machineries. The opening of L.C. is subject to:

i) Deposit of L.C. margin @ 10% of L.C. value subject to change at the time of opening of L.C.

ii) The imported machinery under the L.C. to be cleared by the Bank approval C & F.

iii) Deposit of 100% share certificates of the sponsored directors / promoting share holders of the company to be raised at this stage as collateral security.

iv) Approval of the K.D.A. to set up the Industry at the proposed land.

" A portion of the Ext.18 reads as follows: Penalty: -

If the supplier first party fail to effect the deliveries within the stipulated period they shall be liable to a penalty against their performance Bond at the rate of 2% of the FCB price per day of undelivered stores subject to maximum of 10% (ten percent) the supplier shall not however, be liable for such penalties if delivery’s are delayed by cause beyond their control such as strike, lock out, war, act of God or any other natural causes covered by the term 'Force Majerue'.

13. Now, in this connection let us look to the evidence of PW-1, and DW-1. PW-1, Md. Abul Kashem stated in his cross examination that: কোম্পানী ডাইরেক্টরদের যৌথ স্বাক্ষরে কোন ক্যাশ টাকা ডিসবারস হয় নাই। এল, সি, (বৈদেশিক মুদ্রায়)তে মালামাল সরবরাহকারী কোন টাকা ডিসবার্স করা হয়। এল,সির বিপরীতে টাকা ডিসবার্স করা হয়। সেই এল,সি এখন দেখাইতে পারতেছি না।This witness in his cross-examination also stated that : ১২৫ নং চুক্তিতে ১০ এবং ১৫ নং ক্রমিকে এয়ার ব্লোয়ার এবং এ্যামোনিয়া গ্যাস সরবরাহ করার চুক্তি আছে। ঐ ২টি মাল পৌছাইলে পেমেন্ট করিতাম। ঐ ২টি মালের মুল্য ১০৫০ ইউ,এস, ডলার প্রয়োজন লেখা আছে।

14. DW-1, Md. Ismail Hossain, clearly stated in his evidence that: বাদীর সহিত ২৫/৬/৮৫ তারিখে ৩টি চুক্তি হয় আমাদের। চুক্তি নম্বর ১২৩, ১২৪ ও ১২৫। শর্ত থাকে বাদীপক্ষ চুক্তিতে বর্ণিত মালামাল যন্ত্রপাতি সরবরাহ করিবে। বিনিময়ে প্রডাকশনে গিয়া আমরা টাকা পরিশোধ করিব। চুক্তি থাকে প্রডাকশন-এ গিয়া টাকা পরিশোধযোগ্য হইবে।

15. From the above, it manifests that no cash money was disbursed in favour of the defendant-company for establishment of its Ice Plant and Cold Storage project and as per contract the plaintiff appellant Krishi Bank would supply the machineries on payment of fund in foreign currency for establishment of Ice Plant and Cold Storage project in question.

16. It is found from record that the defendant-respondent has repeatedly requested the plaintiff bank to supply the wanting air blower and Amonia gas for commissioning the project to which the plaintiff-appellant bank could not supply the wanting air blower and Amonia gas as a result of which respondent company could not go into operation of its Ice Plant and Cold Storage project.

17. As we have already noticed that the defendant-respondent No.1 as plaintiff earlier instituted Title Suit No.26 of 1992 in the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Khulna impleading the plaintiff-appellant as defendant No. 5 and others praying for a decree for declaration that the deed of agreement between the parties be cancelled and for recovery of compensation to the tune of Tk. 25 lac. The said suit was decreed in favour of the plaintiff, M/s. Dadajee Ice Plant

and Cold Storage and the said decree was upheld up to the Appellate Division in C.P.L.A. No.191 of 2004, wherein it has been held that:

"In the instant case, the Courts below have considered sections 53 and 54 of the Contract Act and arrived at a finding on material on record that the defendant No.5-petitioner is guilty of non-performance of his part of the contract resulting in causing huge loss to the plaintiff-respondent. It is on record that the plaintiff has repeatedly requested the defendant No. 5-petitioner to provide him the required fund and to supply the wanting air blower and Amonia Gas for commissioning the project to which the defendant No.5-petitioner has left a deaf ear, for which the plaintiff has suffered substantial loss and the trial Court has assessed the compensation at Tk. 25 lac which the Court of appeal below as a final Court of fact has refused to interfere."

18. On an analysis of the evidence of PW-1 and DWI together with the above quoted observation, it is found that the plaintiff-appellant- Bangladesh Krishi Bank is guilty of non-performance of his part of the contract resulting in causing huge loss to the respondent-company.

19. The trial Court below on assessment of the entire evidence on record arrived at a finding that the plaintiff-Bank did not perform his part of contract by importing of all necessary machineries for establishment of his project by the defendant-company and as a result of which the defendant-company sustained huge loss by purchasing the lands in commercial area and constructing factory building. The trial Court also observed that the defendant-company in order to establish his project repeatedly requested the plaintiff-Bank to allow additional fund to the defendant-company and to supply all the materials including Air Blower and Amonia Gas but in spite of that the plaintiff-Bank did not and could not supply all the materials including Air Blower and Amonia Gas for establishment of Ice Plant and Cold Storage project. In the premises aforesaid, we do not think the Artha Rin Adalat committed any wrong in holding that the plaintiff bank could not prove its case.

20. Besides, on top of that the defendant-respondent-company earlier being aggrieved against the appellant bank for non-performance of his part of the contract instituted Title Suit No.26 of 1992 in the first Court of the Subordinate Judge, Khulna impleading the respondent bank as defendant No.5 and other defendants praying for a decree for declaration that the deed of agreement between the parties be cancelled and for recovery of compensation to the tune of Tk.25,00,000/ which was decreed and the same was affirmed up to the Appellate Division in F.A. No.29 of 1996 and C.P.L.A. No.191 of 2004 respectively.

21. However, Mr. Khaled, the learned Advocate for the appellant-Bank repeatedly submitted that the present suit has been filed by the plaintiff-bank only for realization of its outstanding dues which is not at all related or connected with the earlier suit filed by the present respondent- M/s. Dadajee Ice Plant and Cold Storage.

<u>22. To meet this argument, we have carefully studied the judgment of the High Court Division and the Appellate Division passed in F.A. No.29 of 1996 and C.P.L.A. No.191 of 2004 respectively together with the plaints of both the suits including the judgment of the trial Court below and find all the Courts including our Appellate Division consistently held that the appellant-Bank is guilty for non-performance of his part of contract resulting in causing huge loss to the defendant-respondent inasmuch as the appellant-Bank did not fulfill the terms of contract in supplying the entire machineries to the defendant-company and therefore, the respondent-company did not or could not avail to go into operation. Therefore, in the facts and circumstance of the case Mr. Khaled, is not correct in submitting that facts of the instant suit is not at all related or connected with the facts of the earlier suit filed by the present respondent- M/s. Dadajee Ice Plant and Cold Storage.</u>

23. Another aspect of the case must not be overlooked. The trial Court below has come to a finding that the suit was barred by law of limitation in view of the provisions of section 46 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. This finding of the trial Court below is plainly misconceived inasmuch as the instant suit was filed long before the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into force. Mr. Quamrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate for the bank has found himself unable to support this finding of the trial Court.

24. Mr. Khaled, having realised the weakness of the case at the end of the day submits that the case may be sent back on remand to the trial Court for fresh trial.

<u>25. On perusal of the entire materials on record, we find both oral and documentary evidence having been available on record to decide the case on merit and thus, we are of the view that it is not at all justified in sending back the case on remand to the Court below for reconsidering the matter. We are therefore, unable to accept the last submission of Mr. M. Khaled Ahmed.</u>

26. In any view of the matter, having regard to the facts as aforesaid, this appeal must fail. No interference is therefore, called for.

27. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree passed by the Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna in Artha Rin Suit No.103 of 2001 is maintained.

28. Let a copy of the judgment along with lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.

lawyer:
Dr. Rafique Rahman, Senior Advocate, instructed by Azra Ali, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Petitioner 
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondent
