16. The identical prayers were made and sanction letters were issued in respect of almost all the cases of the writ petitioners. It is clear from the undisputed facts that the writ petitioners prayed in the prescribed form to accept their prayers for VRS with immediate effect. The learned Counsel for the writ petitioner-respondents failed to notice any exception. About 10 years thereafter the writ petitioners filed the writ petitions. It is not the case of the writ petitioners that after tendering applications of VRS they filed any application for withdrawal of those applications. On acceptance by the BADC of the request for voluntary retirement made by the writ petitioners their jural relationship ceases.

17. Mr. Bhuyian submits that inspite of withdrawal of benefits, the writ petitioners are entitled to get relief since there can be no waiver of fundamental right of the writ petitioners and estoppel against statute. Estoppel is a bar or impediment preventing a party from assertaining or putting up claim inconsistent with the position, he previously took, either by conduct or words. According to Black's Law Dictionary, in estoppel, a party is prevented by his own act from claiming a right to the detriment of the other party who was entitled to rely on such conduct and has acted accordingly. Submission of Mr. Bhuiyan is correct that there cannot be any estoppel against a statute and such doctrine cannot be used against or in favour of the administration as to give de facto validity to ultra vires administrative acts. But estoppel is a mixed question of law and fact. It appears from the materials on record that in these cases the writ petitioners, in fact, abandoned their right. Firstly by not filing the application for withdrawal of their prayers for VRS. Secondly, by accepting the benefits and incentives. In fact, the writ petitioners intentionally relinquished their rights. The writ petitioners long after making their prayers for voluntary retirement and acceptance of those prayers and receiving financial benefits have filed the writ petitions. They are guilty of acquiesance in accepting the retirement. By not asserting their right in time they allowed it to lapse by delay, latches and acquiescence and accepting the VRS by conduct, the Court cannot come to the rescue of such persons where they themselves withdrew the financial benefits accepting VRS.

18. Mr. Bhuiyan mainly relied upon the provisions of Section 9 of the Public Servants (Retirement) Act, 1974 which run as follows:

"9.Optional retirement-(1) A public servant may opt to retire from service at any time after he has completed twenty five years of service by giving notice in writing to the appointing authority at least thirty days prior to the date of his intended retirement;

Provided that such option once exercised shall be final and shall not be permitted to be modified or withdrawn.

(2) The Government may, if it considers necessary in the public interest so to do, retire from service a public servant at any time after he has completed twenty five years of service without assigning any reason."

19. The aforesaid provisions of the Act is not applicable for the writ petitioners. Voluntary retirement is an early retirement. Incentive is offered to the staffs to reduce workforce and right size the organizations. Such scheme is completely voluntary and different. It is virtually a contract between employer and employees.

20. Section 9 of the Act provides for voluntary retirement from service on completion of 25 years' service by giving notice in writing to the appointing authority at least 30 days prior to the date of his intended retirement. The words "may opt to retire" clearly indicate that the aforesaid provision does not confer on the employee a right to retire. It confers on the employee a right to make an option to permit him to retire. An employee who has put in less number of years of service would not be on better footing than the employee who has put in longer service. The words "opt to retire" indicate that the right which is conferred by it is not the right to retire but a right to ask for retirement. The words "opt to retire" imply a request by the employee and corresponding acceptance by the authority. Here in the case, some of the writ petitioners claimed that since they opted to retire from service before completion of 25 years of service so their option itself was bad in law as such the same was not acceptable and those do not carry any legal validity and those offers were not offers at law. It is upon the authority whether they shall accept such option or not. It cannot be said that an employee retires only on superannuation and there is no other circumstance under which an employee can retire. Retirement on superannuation is not the only mode of retirement known to service jurisprudence. There can be other types of retirements like premature retirement, either compulsory or voluntary. Here the proper authority, accepting those offers, sanctioned the retirement benefits and the writ petitioners withdrew those benefits. Since the appointing authority did not refuse to grant the permission for retirement rather accepted the same their retirement became effective from the date of acceptance. It was, in fact, a contract. The employer offered the proposal and the employees accepted such proposal voluntarily.

21. In the case of ITI Ltd. V. ITI Ex/VR Employees/Officers Welfare Association and others reported in (2010) 12 SCC 347 Supreme Court of India observed that "if an employee has got benefits under the VRS scheme, whether right or wrong, it cannot be reopened....".

22. Moreover, we have considered the whole scheme of VRS and found that there was specific stipulation to the effect, "এই ব্যবস্থা সম্পূর্ণ ঐচ্ছিক। তবে, একবার অবসর গ্রহনের ইচ্ছা প্রকাশ করলে তা পরে প্রত্যাহার করা যাবে না।" That is scheme was purely voluntary and once an option to voluntary retirement is exercised by an employee and the same is accepted by the BADC authority the employee is not entitled to withdraw from voluntary retirement.

<u>23. We have already found that the writ petitioners did not file any application for withdrawal of their prayers for VRS and after 10 years of termination of their service and withdrawal of the pensionaries and other benefits they have filed writ petitions. In all the cases it appears that the writ petitioners themselves by their own conduct abandoned the service in lieu of some consideration. The severance of the relationship of employer and employee takes place immediately on acceptance of the prayers for VRS. The moment their prayers are accepted by the BADC authority their retirement became effective. After 10 years of their voluntary retirement and after receiving full financial benefits as offered the prayers for reinstatement cannot be termed as reasonable and fair. Here, the writ petitioners in their wisdom thought that in view of the situation VRS was a better option available and chose the same. After having applied for VRS and taken the money it is not open to them to contend that they exercised the option under any kind of coercion and undue influence. Who had accepted the ex gratia payment or any other benefit under the scheme, could not have resiled therefrom. It became past and closed transaction. The writ petitioners having accepted the benefit could not be permitted to approbate and reprobate nor they be permitted to resile from their earlier stand.</u>

24. In such view of the matter, our considered opinion is that the writ petitioner-respondents were not entitled to get any relief as prayed for. The High Court Division committed error of law in directing to reinstate the writ petitioner-respondents to their former posts and to pay their back salaries.

25. Accordingly, we find substance in all the appeals.

26. Thus, all the appeals are allowed. The judgment and order of the High Court Division are set aside. The Civil Petitions are disposed of in the light of the decision of the appeals. The review petitions are dismissed accordingly.

End.

parties:
ALI JAN JUTE MILLS LIMITED
Vs.
ALHAJ AHAMMED FAZLUR RAHMAN AND OTHERS
full_judgment:
Khizir Ahmed Choudhury, J: This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1-9 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 19.09.2013 passed by learned District Judge Narshingdi in Title Appeal No. 19 of 2013 allowing the appeal by reversing those dated 21.01.2013 and 24.01.261 3 passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge, Narshingdi Sadar in Title Suit No. 120 of 2003 decreeing the suit should not be set aside.

2. The present petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 120 of 2003 before the Senior Assistant Judge, Narsingdi for declaration that exchange deed No. 11-01 dated 14.01.1986, exchange deed No. 4793 dated 01.05.1987 and disclaimer deed No. 5379 dated 25.05.1987 are illegal, void and not binding, upon the plaintiffs. By filing an application, subsequently the plaintiffs sought for declaration of title over the suit land.

3. The case of the plaintiffs in brief is that Haji Fakir Chand with a view to establish a Jute Mill in the name of his father Ali Jan entered into agreement with the then East Pakistan Industrial Development Corporation on 04.09.1963 and started purchasing lands from many persons and ultimately purchased 39.035 acres of land which became the property of Ali Jan Jute Mills as per the promoter agreement with East Pakistan Government and EPIDC. Thereafter confirmatory agreement was also signed on 30.06.1965. On 05.01.1967 the said Fakir Chand executed a deed of relinquishment for the said 39.035 acres of land in favour of the Mill. The Mill authority after mutating the land in their name, paid Government rent, taxes upto 1480 B.S. and accordingly RS record was prepared in the name of the Ministry of Industries, Government of Bangladesh. The Ali Jan Jute Mills was nationalized on 1972 and after 10 years in 1982, it was denationalized. Within these 10 years some land of jute Mill were leased out. According to registered deed dated 04.12.196-19 an affidavit was sworn before the District registrar regarding the properties to Director of concerned. According to arrangement, East Pakistan industrial Development Corporation got 36.37 percent share, subsequently represented by Ministry of Jute, Government of Bangladesh and rest 63.63 percent share held by heirs of founder namely Ali Jan Jute Mills which is now owned and possessed by present plaintiff Md. Nurul Islam Patwary by, successive transfers. Defendants by 7 registered deeds dated 27.05.1989 transferred 2.9150 acres of land in favour of the plaintiff's predecessor. Defendant No. 1 transferred 6.12 acres of land to his heirs and other co-sharers and also created deeds of exchange and deed of relinquishment which constrained the plaintiff to file the instant suit.

4. The opposite-parties as defendants contested the suit by filing written statement contending inter-alia that with a view to establish Jute Mill, their predecessor Fakir Chand purchased land for Jute Mill who also purchased land in his own name totaling an area of land 39.0350 acres and the said land has been purchased in between 1963 to 1964 AD. Fakir Chand entered into a promoter agreement with East Pakistan Industrial Development Corporation and thereafter on 13.06.1965 executed a confirmatory agreement. An area of 39.0350 acres of land was purchased by Fakir Chand in his own name, as at that time Ali Jan Jute Mills was not established. On 05.01.1967 by an unregistered deed of relinquishment, he transferred 33.234 acres of land in favour of Jute Mill although, actually he transferred 32.0325 acres or land. To secure loan from East Pakistan Industrial Bank, Fakir Chand executed a registered power of attorney being No.17498 on behalf of Ali Jan Jute Mills to give authority to the Bank where also mistakenly land has been shown as 33.234 acres instead of 32.0325 acres; After denationalization and getting possession back by the heirs of the founder Ali Jan Jute Mills Limited, Mr. Fakir Chand, with a view to i remove anomaly, executed 2 deeds in favour of the heirs of Fakir Chand while defendant No. 1 executed 2 deeds of exchange on 14.10.1986 and 30.04.1987 whereby the heirs of Fakir Chand got title and possession regarding the suit land which is situated outside the Jute Mill. On 25.05.1987, a deed of relinquishment was also executed. The heirs of Fakir Chand transferred 32.0350 acres of land in favour of Kazi Mejbah Uddin by 6 registered instruments. On 06.06.1987 a board meeting was held and as per the decision of the board meeting and minutes Kazi Mejbah Uddin admitted the deed oil exchange and a deed of relinquishment and got 32.0325 acres of land as the Mill's property. Kazi Mejbah Uddin, after parching, mortgaged 32.0325 acres of land with Uttara Bank, Matijhil Branch and took loan by executing a, registered irrevocable power of attorney which also contains 32.0325 acres of land. The present plaintiff Md. Nurul Islam Patwary held and possessed the same land. The present plaintiff tried to purchase 6.25 acres of land out of suit land and being unsuccessful filed the instant suit with a view to derive illegal gain.

5. The plaintiffs examined 5 witnesses in support of their claim while the defendants examined 4 witnesses on their behalf. The plaintiffs submitted documentary evidence namely exhibit 1-8. On the other hand the defendants also submitted documentary evidence which have been marked as exhibit Ka-Tha (l).

6. After hearing, the trial Court decreed the suit in favour with the plaintiffs contending that in dealing with company matters, spirit and substance of the provisions are to be looked into and as per promoter's agreement an area of 39.035 acres of land has been transferred in favour of the plaintiffs. Although Fakir Chand executed a deed of disclaimer regarding 32.1275 acres of land in favour of the company but as per promoter's agreement exhibit-2 total land has been transferred. The heirs of Fakir Chand has no right or authority to execute and register the impugned, deeds as after earlier transfer they have no title and interest over the suit land. RS khatian regarding the total quantum of land has been prepared in the name of Ministry of Jute and Ali Jan Jute Mills paid all rents for the entire land. Defendant No. 1 Md. Fazlur Rahman, managing director of the company has no authority to transfer the suit land by the impugned deeds which has not been supported by any resolution of the company and the documentary evidence proves that Fakir Chand transferred his title and interest in favour of the Jute Mill and P.W. 1-4 by giving credible evidence proved the title and possession of the plaintiffs over the suit land.

7. The appellate Court reversed the findings of the trial Court contending that present plaintiff Md. Nurul Islam Pafwary, being managing director of the Ali Jan Jute Mills, purchased the land from Kazi Mejbah Uddin having an area of 32.9150 acres which was also purchased by Kali Mejbah Uddin from the heirs of Fakir Chand. As per the documents it also appears that an area of 2.49 acres of land have been transferred by the heirs of Fakir Chand to 17 other persons in 1986 by registered instrument, but those deeds have not been challenged in the instant proceeding. The defendants transferred an area of 32.9150 acres of land to the plaintiffs and for mere payment of rent and record of right, the company cannot claim any property beyond the land transferred by the defendants and in the plaint it is admitted that rest land beyond, 32.9150 acres of land are in possession of the defendants.

8. Mr. A.F. Hassan Arif, learned Advocate along with learned advocates Mr. T.M. Shakil Hasan, Mr. S.R. Maswod, Mr. Abid Chowdhury and Mr. Moaz Arif, appeared on behalf of the petitioner. Mr. A.F. Hasan Arif, submits that Fakir Chand purchased the entire land for the name and benefit of the company. Although 32.1275 acres of land has been transferred in the name of the company by registered instruments, but on perusal of the promoter's agreement, confirmatory deeds, audit report and other instruments cumulatively, it appears that entire land having purchased by Fakir Chand has been transferred in favour of the company. He next submits that as all the shares of the company have been transferred to the present plaintiffs, certain properties namely the suit land cannot be retained by the original owners. He next submits that the trial Court considered the facts and circumstances and the corporate approach in its true perspective by relying upon the promoter's agreement, confirmatory deeds and other materials namely audit report and found that the entire shares of the company has been transferred in favour of the present plaintiffs and as such the suit land cannot be retained by the defendants. He next submits that the defendant No. 1, the present managing director, has no right or authority to transfer the suit land in favour of the other defendants without taking any decision by board of directors and as such transfer cannot confer title in favour of defendants; He next submits that the witnesses of the plaintiffs elaborately and consistently described the suit land being in possession of the plaintiffs which has been rightly found by the trial Court. The evidence of the plaintiffs are intrinsic in nature which has been rightly appreciated by the trial Court. He next submits that the appellate Court as last Court of fact did not reverse the findings and reasonings put forward by the Court of I instance in its true perspective and thereby arrived at a wrong conclusion which cannot be sustained. Mr. Arif further submits that the company is a juristic person and the shares and all other stock and trade are vested to the company by transfer of shares, all the assets stock in trade and other assets of the company vested to the transferees. Referring clause 4 and other clauses of the confirmatory agreement, Mr. Arif submits that it is specifically mentioned therein that lands appertaining thereto and all stock in trade, book debts and other assets and liabilities including the benefit of all subsisting contracts in respect thereof shall be acquired by the company as shown in the balance sheet made upto 30th day of June 1965 and as such although there is no specific mention about the total quantum of land, but in fact all the lands of the companies stood vested to the transferees and as such the transfers made by, defendant No. 1 to other defendants by the impugned deeds conferred no title upon the recipient of the documents. He furthers submits that the findings and reasonings of the appellate Court is not a proper reversal under Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such the appellate Court without considering the facts and circumstances and legal point vis-a-vis the company matter in its true perspectives, arrived at a wrong conclusion simply considering the deed of transfers as sale deed. He further submits that the entire land purchased by Fakir Chand constituted a single unit and when the property have been nationalized, all the properties have been taken over and when it was denationalized again, it has been denationalized as a whole and as such the suit land cannot be separated from the other land. He further submits that the findings of the appellate Court does not cover all gamut of factual aspects as well as legal approach and the appellate Court also i failed to discuss the evidence in its true perspectives and as such for effectual adjudication and disposal of the suit, if necessary the suit can be sent on remand to the appellate Court. Mr. Arif in support of his contention referred the case of Md. Golam Sarwar and others -vs- Md. Liakat Ali and others reported in 18 BLD (AD)-15, Md. Afazuddin Mollah and others -vs- Moyezuddin Sheikh being. dead his heirs 1985 BLD (AD)-54 and Johara Khatun and others -vs- Md. Habib Khan and another reported in 15 BLD (AD)-120.

9. Mr. A.M. Amin Uddin, learned Advocate, Mr. Qamrul Haque Siddique learned advocate along with Mr. Samarendra Nath Biswas, advocate and Mr. Md. Adnan Sarker learned Advocate appeared for the opposite parties. Mr. Qamrul Haque Siddique submits that the original owner Fakir Chand purchased the suit land along with other land totalling an area of 39.0350 acres by various registered deeds and out of the said purchased land 32.9150, acres of land has been transferred in favour of the company by a deed of disclaimer and as such the company cannot claim any other land beyond 32.9150 acres of land. He further submits that although in the deed of disclaimer 33.9150 acres of land have been mentioned, but in fact 32.9150 acres of land has been approved as the property of the company which has been confirmed in various board meetings. He next submits that by executing registered power of attorneys by original owner Fakir Chand subsequently Kazi Mejbah Uddin and presently the present, managing director Nurul Islam Patwary obtained loans from various Bank showing the land of the company as being 32.9150-acres and as such raising claim beyond the transferred land cannot be sustained by any stretch of imagination. He next submits that promoter's agreement confirmatory agreement, memorandum and other deeds are not registered instrument and any immovable property, cannot be transferred without any registered instrument. Since the assets of the company has been transferred as per company law, the exact area have been transferred in favour of the company by deed of disclaimer which is within the boundary of the company. He next submits that late Fakir Chand has purchased the land having area of 39.9150 acres by various registered deeds before floating the company in Question and as such the property acquired by Fakir Chand in his individual capacity cannot be claimed as property of the company without any express covenant executed by the owner in favour of the company. He next submits that defendant No. 1, the managing director of company has transferred the suit land by virtue of exchange deed and the deed of the disclaimer which has been approved by board meeting dated 06.06.1987 exhibit- Gha-1 and as such the present managing director and other directors of the board of the company cannot claim the suit land as property of the company. He next submits that the mortgage deed executed by Kazi Mejbah Uddin in favour of the Bank as well as the mortgage deed executed by the present managing director Nurul Islam Patwary in favour of the Bank, the property of the company has been shown as 32.915.0 acres and as such from these documents it can be clearly inferred that the actual quantum of land vested in favour of the company as shown in the mortgage deeds. He next submits that present managing director Nurul Islam Patwary has purchased the suit land from Kazi Mejbah Uddin who obtained the assets of the company by disclaimer agreement and as such the present owner or the managing director as the case may be, cannot claim any land beyond his purchase land and the land purchase by his previous owner Kazi Mejbah Uddin. He submits that the witnesses of the plaintiffs failed to substantiate their claim beyond purchased land by Dying any cogent evidence. He next submits that the plaintiff has got no legal character to initiate the suit which is barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act in absence of further relief or consequential relief as the case may be and simple suit for declaration filed seeking i negative prayers is not maintainable in the facts and circumstances of the instant case. He next submits that nowhere in the promoter's agreement, confirmatory, agreement and any other deeds there is mention of suit land to be acquired by the company and as such relying upon those deeds they will not get any benefit. He finally submits that the trial Court, without considering and appreciating the factual aspect of the case, decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs relying upon promoter's agreements, confirmatory agreement and other documents by misinterpreting the relevant documents, but the appellate Court as last Court of facts considered all facts and circumstance as well as legal provisions and. rightly dismissed the suit by reversing the judgment of the trial Court which cannot be taken exception to and as such the rule bears no substance.

10. Having gone through the pleadings documents oral evidence and judgment of both the Courts below it appears that Fakir Chand purchased the property having area of 39.035 acres of land by various registered instrument. Out of those documents, in some documents the purpose of purchasing the suit land has been shown to establish Ali Jan Jute Mills and in some documents it has been mentioned that Fakir Chand can use the suit land for his individual purpose or the purpose of the company and some documents recites that Fakir Chand simply purchased the suit land and he will be entitled to hold and possess the same peaceably and uninterruptedly without any let or hindrance. Although it is not asserted how much land has been purchased for the company but it is certain that Fakir Chand did not purchase all the properties for use and occupation of the company. It is certain that subsequently fakir Chand established a company namely Ali Jan Jute Mills and entered into promoter's agreement with East Pakistan Industrial. Development Corporation where the shares of the respective parties has been delineated. Subsequently Fakir Chand executed and registered a power of attorney and also executed a deed of disclaimer wherein 32.9150 acres of land has been mentioned as having transferred in favour of the company. Meanwhile, property has been nationalized and subsequently it has been denationalized and by virtue of the denationalization, Fakir Chand again continued to manage and hold the company and while holding and possessing, transferred it to Kazi Mejbah Uddin and by successive transfers, now being held and possessed by the present managing, director Nurul Islam Patwary. On perusal of the documents in question namely, the deed of disclaimer, power of attorney, promoter's agreement, confirmatory agreement, audit report, resolution of the board of directors, total quantum of land having transferred in favour of the company is not beyond 32.9150 acres of land.

11. Regarding the submissions of Mr. A. F. Hassan Arif that all the properties having acquired by Fakir Chand stood vested to the company and since the entire shares and debentures of the company have been transferred in favour of the plaintiff, all the properties acquired by Fakir Chand also stood vested in favour of the company, but as it is found on perusal of the documents namely the purchase deed of Fakir Chand, that Fakir Chand purchased the property by various registered instrument, where certain property was purchased for the establishment of company and remaining property was purchased for personal use and in that event the remarks of the promoter's agreement as well as the confirmatory agreement does not support the plea that all the properties purchased by Fakir Chand stood transferred in favour of the company by operation of law. The trial Court by relying upon the promoter's agreement and confirmatory agreement decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs holding that in company matter, the promoter's agreement as well as confirmatory agreement have got primacy over, all other instrument and as such the trial Court was inclined to decree the suit.

12. The trial Court committed fundamental. error .without considering the facts that Fakir Chand purchased certain portion of land for his personal use and occupation and for certain land, he had the option to use it for company or for himself and as such this property also cannot be considered as property of the company in absence of express relinquishment by Fakir Chand, the owner of the land in question. Even, it is assumed for arguments that in the company matters, promoter agreement and confirmatory agreement as referred by the trial Court have primacy over. all other instrument, even then, the land question have been mentioned in various board meeting having transferred in favour of the company as 32.9150 acres and the plea is further bolstered on perusal of the power of attorney and other instrument executed by Fakir Chand, Kazi Mejbah Uddin and Nurul Islam Patwary. So, by no stretch of imagination it cannot be held that all the properties purchased by Fakir Chand stood transferred in favour of the company.

<u>13. So far the nationalization and denationalization of the company and holding shares by the stake holders are concerned, there is no disputes between the parties. Regard the submission of Mr. Hassan Arif that all die properties having purchased by Fakir Chand stood transferred in favour of the present management of the company by operation of law as the company is a juristic person, such submission could have been substantiated, had all the properties been acquired by Fakir Chand for establishment of the company and as such his argument of transfer of suit land to company by operation of law has no legs to stand upon. The trial Court failed to advert towards the contents of registered instrument purchased by late Fakir Chand vis-a-vis the contents of the promoter's agreement, confirmatory agreement and other deeds and thereby arrived at a wrong conclusion that by confirmatory agreement and promoters agreement the suit land stood vested in favour of the company.</u>

<u>14. The trial Court also committed error in relying upon the record of right and payment of rent which tempted it to arrive at a conclusion that Fakir Chand or his heirs lost their interest in the suit land. It is fairly established that for mere preparation of record of right without having no support of credible document one cannot claim ownership over that land. Onus of record of right is rebuttable presumption which can be rebutted by showing credible document and in the instant case the defendants have been able to show that record of right of the entire land has been wrongly prepared in the name of the plaintiffs.</u>

<u>15. The appellate Court dealt with all aspects of the case and reversed the findings of the trial Court. The appellate Court also discussed the evidence of the witnesses and specially pointing the evidence of P.W-1 the appellate Court found that P.W- 1 admitted that the suit land is out of the boundary of the company and has not been included in the deeds in question. On perusal of the evidence of the witnesses it also appears that P.W-1 admitted that the suit land stands outside the boundary wall of the company and there are some other lands namely 2 acres land situated at Mouja Sathilpara is also beyond the claim of the plaintiff. P.W-4 and P.W-5 claimed themselves as lessee of the suit land for particular periods, but in their cross-examination they failed to mention exact plot numbers and also failed to produce their documents in support of their claim of lease.</u>

16. In 1985 BLD AD 54 as referred by Mr. Hassan Arif it is held that reversal of the trial Court's judgment, without adverting to the evidence on which trial Court's judgment is based is not a proper judgment of reversal and in that event High Court Division can interfere therein. Similar view has been reiterated in 18 BLD AD 15 and 15 BLD AD 120 but in the instant case the appellate Court upon consideration of factual and legal aspect as well as evidence on record reversed the decision of the trial Court, so the ratio as referred by Mr. Arif is not applicable in the instant case.

17. Regarding the submission of Mr. Qamrul Haque Siddique that this suit is not maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act for not seeking further relief or consequential relief, as the case may be, it appears that the plaintiffs subsequently by amending the plaint, inserted prayer for declaration of title and as such it cannot be said that the suit is not maintainable in its present form as further relief has been sought. After amendment, the relief sought for regarding the impugned deeds became consequential relief. Apart from this, in appropriate case a prayer with negative declaration is maintainable provided the plaintiffs have got their title and possession in the suit land but in the instant case the plaintiffs have sought declaration of title as well as they challenged the documents whereby the defendants have transferred the land in question in favour of the other defendants. So, the instant suit is maintainable given the facts and circumstances of the case.

18. Regarding the submission of Mr. Hassan Arif and the decision as referred by him, regarding remand, 'it appears that the suit or appeal can be remanded to the respective Courts if detailed discussion of evidence by the Court concerned is lacking or for which the disputes cannot be completely and effectually adjudicated, but in the instant case it is found from the record that the parties have furnished both oral and documentary evidence to the hilt and the evidence both oral and documentary have been taken into consideration to arrive at a decision by the appellate Court and as such there arise no occasion for remanding the appeal to the appellate Court.

19. In the above facts and circumstances, it is my considered view that the trial Court without considering the legal aspect and factual scenarios decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff, but the appellate Court considering all aspects of the case rightly reversed the findings of the trial Court.

20. In the above context, I find no merit in the rule and accordingly, the rule is discharged without any order as to cost.

21. Let a copy of the judgment along with the lower Court record be sent to the concerned Court.

End.

full_judgment:
Md. Nuruzzaman, J. The instant Appeal is directed against the Judgment and decree dated 27.06.2010 and 05.07.2010 respectively at the instance of the plaintiff passed by Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 264 of 2007 dismissing the suit.

2. The material facts relevant, for disposal of the instant First Appeal, succinctly, are that, the defendant No. 1 is the permanent citizen of Bangladesh and has been serving as Officer in the Arab Bangladesh Bank Limited. Moulana Mohammad Salem Wahedi was his father who had been appointed as Nikah Registrar in the year of 1961. He had a good reputation as Marriage Registrar. The said Salem Wahedi purchased a property in the name of the defendant No. 1, as father vide registered deed No. 7416 of 1964 dated 11.08.1964 from the lease holder one Allahrakha Ansari who got the same from the government of erstwhile East Pakistan vide registered lease deed No. 5825 of 1963.

3. The defendant No. 1 Mohammad Obaidullah @ Obaidullah Aslam left the suit property at the time of liberation war due to abnormal situation at Mirpur Area. In the absence of defendant No. 1 some persons occupied the property and possessed the suit property collusively with the help of staff of the Deputy Commissioner Office. They treated the suit land as abandoned property vide Gazette notification dated 23.09.1986 which was published by the Ministry of Housing and Public Works. Thereafter, Mr. Mohammad Obaidullah @ Obaidullah Aslam the defendant No. 1 made numerous applications to the concerned departments and authorities for exclusion of the suit property form "KA" list but in vain. Thereafter, the defendant No. 1 Mr. Obaidullah filed an application in the Court of Settlement, Segunbagicha, Dhaka which was registered as Settlement Case No. 55 of 1991. The aforementioned Settlement Case was heard by the Court of Settlement presiding over Mr. Khandker Musa Khaled as chairman. The Court of settlement upon hearing both the sides by its Judgment dated 05.12.1995 excluded the suit property from the "KA" list of abandoned building and further declared that the petitioner is entitled to return back the possession of the house immediately.

4. The defendant No. 1 Mr. Mohammad Obaidullah @ Obaidullah As lam on 23.01.2006 executed and registered an irrevocable Power of Attorney in favour of Alhaj M.N.A. Afgani to do all the necessary works regarding the suit property on his behalf. Mr. Mohammad Obaidullah Obaidullah Aslam on 04.05.2006 through legally constituted attorney executed a sale deed of agreement for sale of the suit property in favour of Mrs. Mosammat Amena Begum receiving Taka 7,00,000/- (Seven lac) out of total consideration money of Tk. 7,50,000/-(Seven lac fifty thousand).

5. The deed of agreement for sale was registered on 04.06.2006 being deed No. 3432. On 01.04.200.7 Mr. Mohammad Obaidullah Salim through attorney receipt Tk. 30,000/- (Thirty Thousand) out of rest of consideration money Tk. 50,000/- (Fifty thousand) and handed over the possession of the suit property to the plaintiff Musammat Amena Begum in presence of witnesses on promise to register the deed of sale either himself or through his Attorney very soon on receipt of balance of Tk. 20,000/- (Twenty thousand).

6. The purchaser due to delay the registration of the sale deed took over the possession of the suit property from D.N.A. holder occupant Md. Hafizur Rahman and obtained a written deed from attorney Alhaj M.N.A Afgani and she also got the delivery of possession of all the original documents. The plaintiff according to the deed of agreement of sale offer the balance money of Tk. 20,000/- (Twenty thousand) on 29/30 Oct 2007 to the Attorney of defendant No. 1 and requested him to execute and register the deed of sale in favour of the plaintiff. However, Mr. M.N.A Afgani the attorney of the vendor took dilatory tactic on the various pretend and said that he would execute and register the sale deed after some days. The plaintiff when ask him to fix a specific day but he declined to say the fix date of registration, not any that all on a sudden at the time of conversation he told that he will not execute and register the sale deed. Due to such activities of the Attorney of defendant No. 1 the plaintiff has not been able to register the deed of sale. In the mean time the plaintiff came to learn on a reliable source that the defendant No. 1 and his Attorney for illegal gain most illegally trying to sell the suit property to the other person depriving the plaintiff from his legal and legitimate claim and right. The plaintiff while residing in the suit property some purchaser had come to see the house to purchase the property. In such facts and circumstances the plaintiffs was in serious doubt that she would be ousted and further more sufferer due to illegal steps of the defendant No.1 and his Attorney. The plaintiff having no other alternative but has been compelled to file the suit for Specific Performance of Contract and permanent injunction against the defendants. 7. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the statement made in paragraph 1 to 8 are matter of records and the plaintiff is put to strict prove of the case however, they have believed that the value of the suit property is more then 7,50,000/- (Seven Lac and fifty thousand) as it was decided on 04.05.2006 through registered deed of agreement however, in the facts of the case of the written statement the Attorney of the defendant No. 1 himself admit the facts of contract for sale. But he claimed Tk. 1,00,000/-(One lac) extra for increasing the value of the suit with rest Tk. 20,000/- (Twenty thousand) in total 1,20,000/-(One lac and twenty thousand) for execution and registration of the sale deed within 2/3 months.

8. The learned Joint District on perusal of the pleadings of, both the sides framed the following issues:

1) Whether the suit is maintainable in its present form and manner ?

2) Whether the claim of the plaintiff is correct or not ?

3) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get the relief as prayed for ?

9. The plaintiff to prove his plaint case examined 4 witnesses. P.W. 1 A.K.M. Hafizur Rahman, P.W. 2 Haji Hossen, P.W. 3 Bodiuzzaman, P.W. 4 Md. Nurul Amin. The plaintiff side to prove the case also produced some documentary evidences which have been marked as exhibits. Power of Attorney dated 10.09.2009 is exhibit -1, Judgment of Settlement case No. 55 of 1991 is exhibit -2. Deed No. 7416 dated 11.08.1964 is exhibit-3, lease deed No. 5825 dated 16.04.1963 is exhibit-4, deed of agreement for sale dated 04.06.2006 is exhibit- 5 and 5(1), the deed of agreement for possession and receipt of Tk. Exhibit -6, the deed of possession handed over to the plaintiff is exhibit-7, Death Certificate dated 12.04.1954 is exhibit-8, citizen certificate in the name of Md. Obaidullah is exhibit-9, letter of possession in favour of Allahrakha is exhibit -10, Death Certificate of Allahrakha Ansari is exhibit -11.

10. On the other hand, the defendant to substantiate the defence case as narrated in the written statement examined 2 witnesses. D.W.1 M.N.A. Afgani, D.W.2 Adv. Chowdhury Wahidur Rahman. The defendants side also produced some documentary evidences which have been marked as exhibits. Exhibit -Ka Power of Attorney dated 23.01.2006, Exhibit- Kha Letter of Administrative officer vide No. 745 dated 27.07.1964, Exhibit Ga to Ga (14) Bill of Dhaka Eclectic Supply, Exhibit Gha, Gha (1) and Gha (2) Certificate upon Form-A, Exhibit — Uma and Uma (1) Notices of case No. 55 of 1991 dated 01.10.1991, Exhibit — Cha Voter list, Exhibit — Chaa Letter dated 29.03.1978, Exhibit — Ja Letter dated 05.07.1978.

11. The learned Joint District Judge, Arbitration Adalat by his Judgment and decree dated 27.06.2010 and 05.07.2010 respectively passed in Title Suit No. 264 of 2007 dismissing the suit on contest against the defendant No. 1 and ex-parte against the rest defendants.

12. The plaintiff feeling aggrieved by the Judgment and decree dated 27.06.2010 and 05.07.201 respectively passed in Title Suit No. 264 of 2007 preferred the instant First Appeal before this Court.

13. At first we shall meticulously examine the testimonies of all the P.Ws. and D.Ws. Thereafter, we shall discussed the legality and pro-priority of the documentary evidences to come on a definite findings.

14. Mr. A.K.M. Hafizur Rahman P.W.1 has testified that he is husband and Attorney of the plaintiff. He has produced the Power of Attorney which is exhibit-1. The defendant No. 1 is the owner of the suit land and suit was filed for Specific Performance of Contract and permanent injunction. The defendant No. 1 is a permanent citizen of Bangladesh by Birth who has been serving in the Arab Bangladesh Bank Limited as an Officer. He is the son of Moulana Mohammad Salem Wahedi who was the Nikah Registrar of Sutrapur area. He was appointed in the year of 1961 and working till day. He knows the Sister and Brother of the defendant and they are elite of the society. In the year of 1948 while defendant No. 1 was minor his father Kazi Saheb purchased the suit land through registered sale deed in the name of defendant No. 1. The said deed has been lying with him. Allahrakha Ansari got the lease from the government. Allahrakha Ansari obtained the income tax clearance and transferred the same to the defendant No. 1. The Original lease deed was in the name of the Allahrakha Ansari, the government handed over the possession to Allahrakha Ansari.

15. The defendant No. 1 has been owning and possessing the suit property. The defendant No. 1 left the suit property during the liberation war for unavoidable situation therefore, the suit property becomes the abandoned property. The defendant No. 1 time and again filed the applications for recovery of the suit property. Thereafter, the defendant No. 1 filed a case to the Court of Settlement for exclusion of the suit property and obtained order in his favour. In this way, the suit property was released from the list of the abandoned property. There was a order to hand over the possession of the property. He got the Judgment of the Court of Settlement in his favour and there is a settlement in respect of papers and case of the Court of settlement.

16. The government did not file any appeal against the judgment of the Court of settlement therefore; the Judgment of the Court of settlement becomes absolute. On 23.01.2006 the defendant No. 1 appointed Mr. M.N.A Afgani as Attorney to look after the property and do others necessary work. The said Power of Attorney was registered in the Mirpur Sub-Registrar Office. The Power of Attorney on 04.05.2006 made an agreement for sale which was executed and registered on the same day fixing the value of the property Tk. 7,50,000/- (Seven lac fifty thousand) out of which the Attorney received Tk. 7,00,000/-(Seven lac). The deed of agreement being No. 3432 dated 04.06.2006 is lying with plaintiff No. 1.

17. On 28.02.2007 the defendant No. 1 through - Attorney had given the letter of Apush Nama (zitt9M 1"41t) to the plaintiff receiving Tk. 30,000/- (Thirty thousand) out of rest Tk. 50,000/- (Fifty thousand). There is a letter of Acknowledgement. There was a settlement to register the sale deed within 13.10.2007. He has submitted the certified copy of the Judgment of settlement Court dated 05.12.1995 passed in Settlement Case No. 55 of 1991. He has submitted the original deed being No. 7416 dated 11.08.1963 exhibit — 3, exhibit — 4 is the original lease deed being No. 5825 dated 16.04.1963 in the name of Allahrakh Ansari. The deed of Baina Nama dated 04.05.2006 being No. 3432 exhibit — 5 (with objection). Exhibit — 6 is the letter of possession dated 01.04.2007, Exhibit — 7 is the letter of possession dated 28.02.2007. Exhibit — 8 is the birth certificate of defendant No.1. He has submitted the photocopy of the appointment letter of the father of defendant No. 1, exhibit — 9 is the original citizen certificate issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs with forwarding letter. He requested the Attorney of defendant No. 1 to execute and register the sale deed. He was ready to pay the rest of Tk. 20,000/- and till now he is ready to pay the said money. The defendant No. 1 and his attorney trying to sold out the suit property to other persons. Some buyer came in the suit property to see it. The Attorney has no right to sell the property to other person. He has submitted the document of possession dated 03.07.1963 which is exhibit — 10. Exhibit — 11 is the certified copy of the death certificate of Allahrakha Ansari. Not a fact that there was talk to pay of Tk. 1,20,000/- (One lac twenty thousand) and if he paid the same then deed will execute. He prayed for decree for Specific Performance of Contract on behalf of defendant No. 1.

18. In cross: P.W.1 replied that he was a government servant now he is in retirement. Not a fact that there was a conversation to pay Tk. 1,00,000/- (One lac) in addition of consideration money. Not a fact that the story of sell of the of the suit property to other person is false. Not a fact that if pay additional Taka 1,00,000/- (One lac) instead of filing the suit, then he would have the deed.

19. P.W.2 — Hazi Hossain. He knows the plaintiff and defendants. The suit plot is house No. 6-D, 5/18. Deed of agreement for sale was made on 04.05.2006 between the parties. He was the witness to the Bainanama dated 04.05.2006. He has signed in the Bainanama. This is his signature exhibit —5/1. At the time of registration of the Bainanama Tk. 7,00,000/- (Seven lac) was paid by the plaintiff.

20. In cross he replied that he has come in the Court on receiving the summon. He did not know whether after the Baina Nama there was a discussion among the parties regarding the financial matters.

21. P.W.3 — Bodiuzzaman. He knows the plaintiff and defendant. On 04.05.2006 he has signed in the Baina Patra being No. 3432 and his signature in the Baina Patra is exhibit —5(2). He is the scribe. The deed of agreement was written in his office. The price was Tk. 7,50,000/- out of consideration money 7,00,000/- (Seven lac) has been paid.

22. In cross: he replied that he sit in the Sub-Registered Office at Mirpur. He has come to the Court today on receiving the summon. He did not know about the financial transaction after the Bainanama.

23. P.W.4 — Md. Nurul Amin. He knows the plaintiff and defendant. In his presence on 01.04.2007 the defendant handed over the possession of the suit property to the plaintiff. He has signed in the deed of possession as witness. The plaintiff in his presence paid Tk. 30,000/- (Thirty thousand) to the defendant.

24. In Cross- he replied that he did not know whether there is a conversation on behalf of the defendant to pay Tk. 1,00,000/-(One lac) in addition of remaining money 20,000/-(Twenty thousand). It was stipulated that the rest of the money would be paid at the time of handing over the possession. Not a fact that he did not know about the payment of the plaintiff. Not a fact that he has testified falsely.

25. D.W.1 —M.N.A. Afgani. He testified that he is the Attorney of defendant No. 1. Allahrakha Ansari was the original owner of the suit property. Allahrakha Ansari got the suit property on 16.041963 vide deed No. 5825. On 11.8.1964 Allahrakha Ansari transferred the suit property to the defendant No. 1 vide deed being No. 7416. Allahrakha Ansari has paid the government dues. The suit property was purchased in the name of defendant No. 1 by his father. At the time of

liberation war in 1971 the defendant No. 1 resided in the suit property. Due to fear of life he left the resident and went to Kalotola, Sutrapur (কলুটোলা, সূত্রাপুর) । After liberation he went to the suit property and saw some trespassers possessed the property. They had listed the suit property as an abandoned property. After liberation the father of defendant No. 1 made numerous applications to the government for release of the suit property but all were in vain. Thereafter, he unsuccessfully filed the case being Settlement Case No. 55 of 1991 in the Court of Settlement Court No. 1. On 05.12.1995 the Court of Settlement passed the Judgment and order excluding the suit property from the list of abandoned property and directed the government to hand over the possession of the suit property to the defendant No. 1. The government did not file any appeal or writ against the said Judgment of the Court of Settlement. The defendant No. 1 made a registered Power of Attorney being No. 381 in his name. The Attorney on behalf of the defendant No. 1 made a registered Bainapatra on 04.05.2006 receiving Tk. 7,00,000/-(Seven lac) out of total consideration of Tk. 7,50,000/- (Seven lac and fifty thousand). On 08.02.2007 he got possession of the suit property. On 01.04.2007 he handed over the possession to the plaintiff. In the same day he got Tk. 30,000/-(Thirty thousand) from the plaintiff out of remaining Tk. 50,000/- (Fifty thousand). He has claimed Tk. 1,00,000/-(One lac) more for register of the suit property at the ending of October 2007. At the instance of defendant No. 1 the plaintiff was agreed to pay the said money. He demand Tk. 1,20,000/-(One lac and twenty thousand) however, the plaintiff filed the suit without payment of Tk. 1,20,000/-(One lac and twenty thousand). The plaintiff if paid Tk. 1,20,000/-(One lac and twenty thousand) he would have registered the deed in that case there would be no cause of action for filing the suit. The plaintiff filed the suit due to misunderstanding and there is no cause of action to file the suit. The defendant No. 1 now has been serving Arab Bangladesh Bank under Bongshal Branch. He prays for dismissal of the suit. He submitted the Power of Attorney dated 23.01.2006 being No. 381 which has been marked as exhibit `Ka'. He has produced the letter being No. 745 dated 27.07.1964 which has been marked as exhibit `Kha'. He has produced electricity bill of 15 pieces which has been marked exhibit 'Ga.'. He has filed the certificate in form — A which has been marked as exhibit `Gha'. He has produced the 2nd notice of the Case No. 55 of 1991 which has been marked as exhibit 'Uma'. He has produced 01 copy of notice which has been marked as exhibit Cha. He has produced the letter vide memo No. AB-282/75 I 229(1) dated 29.03.1978 which has been marked exhibit ‘Chha (ছ)’. He has produced the letter dated 05.07.1978 being memo No. 93 (নি-২) which has been marked as exhibit `Ja (জ)'.

26. In cross — he replied that the signature of the defendant No. 1 has identified by Advocate Chowdhury Wahidur Rahman. He has given the documents to the plaintiffs. Allahrakha Ansari died on 02.06.1967. Not a fact that demand of additional Tk. 1,00,000/-(One lac) is illegal. Not a fact that he has deposed falsely.

27. D.W.2 — Chowdhury Wahidur Rahman Advocate — He has stated that the draft of Power of Attorney made by him. He has identified the signature of defendant No. 1. The defendant No. 1 has signed in his presence. He has signed in the page No. 8 of the power of attorney which has been marked exhibit — Ka (1). He has signed in the Power of Attorney No. 381 as identifier and he has signed in the Power of Attorney which has been marked exhibit — Ka(2). No. Cross.

28. Mr. Deb Das Sammaddar has submitted that the plaintiff produced all the documentary evidences to prove the plaint case including the deed of agreement for sale as well as registered Power of Attorney. Mr. Sammaddar has further submitted that the trial Court misread and misconstrued the evidences on record thereby failed to consider all the exhibits in its true perspective. He has added that not only that the Court below misread the exhibit '2' in not considering the same as certified copy of Court of Settlement and, as such, judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He has further added that the suit is for Specific Performance of Contract and permanent injunction wherein the plaintiff was able to prove the transaction of Bainanama including handing over the possession of the suit property and original deed of vendor. So, the learned Judge erred in law in dismissing the suit. In support of his submission he cited some precedences which are to the case of the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Public Works Vs. The Chairman, Court of Settlement and others reported 17 B.L.D (AD) 301, to the case of Nitai Ch. Shaha Vs. M/S City Ice and Cold Storage Ltd and others reported 35 D.L.R -60, to the case of Nurul Islam and others V. Jamila Khatun and others reported in 53 D.L.R (AD) 45, to the case of Akbar Hossain (Md) Vs. Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Housing and Works reported 48 D.L.R (HCD) 191.

29. We have gone through the plaint, written statement all the testimonies of P.Ws. and D.Ws and documentary evidences produced by P.W.-1. Exhibit '1' is the Power of Attorney affirmed before the Notary Public on 10.09.2009. Exhibit '2' the Judgment of the Court of Settlement passed in case No. 55 of 1991 (Ka — 236 — Mirpur, Dhaka), the deed dated 11 August 1964 exhibit '3'. The Sketch map exhibit '4', deed of agreement for sale dated 4th May 2006 executed by M.N.A. Afgani on behalf of his principle Md. Obaidullah Salem in favour of Mrs. Amena Begum wife of A.K.M. Hafizur Rahman exhibit '5', exhibit '6' is deed of handing over the possession of the property and money receipt dated 01.04.2007, exhibit '7' is the deed of handing over the possession by one Hafizur Rahman in favour of Md. Obaidullah Saleh alias Aslam, exhibit '8' is the Birth Certificate fathers name of Salim dated 29 December 1997, exhibit '9' is the application to the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs dated 08.03.1978, exhibit '10' is the letter vide memo No. 2905 dated 05.06.1963, exhibit '11' is the death certificate of Allahrakha Ansari dated 05.07.1983.

30. On sifting the oral evidences of P.Ws. it appear that P.W.-1 A.K.M. Hafizur Rahman, son of Unus Mia of house No. 18, Road No. 5, Block — D, Mirpur Section — 6 Dhaka. One perusal of the Power of Attorney exhibit — 1 it appears that the said P.W.- is none but the husband of the plaintiff who also made the deed of agreement of possession handing over the suit property to his wife stating his name as Md. Hafizur Rahman however, the present address and father name and permanent address given in the exhibit '8' and address of others documentary evidences i.e. exhibit '7', '6' and exhibit '1' are the same. So, it is proved through documentary evidences that the handing over of possession of the suit property to the plaintiff not by the government but P.W-1 who is none but her husband. On cross examination he admitted that he was a government officer however, he has concealed the facts that he was a DNA holder of the government and in connivance with the defendant No.1 prepared a Power of Attorney. Thereafter, through Power of Attorney he made a deed of agreement for sale of the suit property in the name none but his wife, therefore, we have no hesitation to opine that the P.W.1 has made the document i.e. sale of agreement and agreement of handing over the possession of the suit property with connivance in favour of his wife to grab same.

31. But facts remains that through exhibit `2' Judgment of the Settlement Court they never got possession from the government. The ownership of the original owner was not denied by the government but admittedly the property was listed in the "Ka" list of the abandoned property which proved that the defendant No. 1 was/is not possessed in the suit property. So, we find that the suit property was never possessed by the defendant No. 1. More-so, it appears from the record that deed of agreement for sale registered on 04.05.2006 and filing of the suit on 29.11.2007.

32. Therefore, it is crystal clear that the instant suit was instituted long after 1 year. According to the last amendment of Article 113 of the Limitation Act made in the year 2004 limitation for filing the suit for Specific Performance of Contract is 1 (one) year from the date of execution and registration of the deed of sale agreement.

33. Furthermore, the provision of section 21A of the Specific Relief Act speaks the suit for Specific Performance of Contract must be instituted by depositing the balance amount of consideration money in the Court at the time of filing of the suit, otherwise, the suit would not be registered but if so registered and proceeded that would be flagrant violation of the provision of section 21A of the Registration Act.

34. For the ready reference and convenience of the discussions we may s reproduced the provision of section 21A Specific Relief Act and Article 113 of the Limitation Act which runs as follows:

35. 21A. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Act or any other law for the time being in force, no contract for sale of any immovable property can be specifically enforced unless —

(a) the contract is in writing and registered under the Registration Act, 1908, whether or not the transferee has taken possession of the property or any part thereof; and

(b) the balance amount of considerations of the contract is deposited in the court at the time of filing the suit for specific performance of the contract. ]

(C) Of the discretion of the Court.

Article —113 of the Limitation Act:

113 For specific performance of a contract [One year] The date fixed for the performance, or, if no such date is fixed, when the plaintiff has notice that performance is refused.

36. On perusal of the provision as quoted herein above we find that the suit was filed after expiry of the limitation and in violation of section 21A of the Specific Relief Act. It has been provided in the provision of section 21A the balance amount of consideration must be deposited at the time of filing of the suit which is mandatory therefore, we find that the suit has been filed in violation of the above law and, as such, the suit is not maintainable and the plaintiff is not entitled to have the decree for Specific Performance of Contract.

<u>37. More-so, from the Judgment of the Court below it appears that the learned Judge after consideration of the documentary evidence came to the conclusion that the handing over the possession and preparation of the documents is anything but concocted papers. We find that the preparation and registration of Bainanama by dint of Power of Attorney is not proved because neither the principal was examined to prove the Power of Attorney nor the Power of Attorney in original was produced in Court. So, the power of attorney has not been marked as exhibit to proof the genuineness of it in accordance with law. We are, therefore, of the considered view that the plaintiff has failed to prove the basis of the Bainanama in accordance with law. It is our further opinion that there is no legal and lawful error nor the Judgment and decree passed by the Court below is tainted or suffers from legal infirmity which does not call any interferences by this Court.</u>

<u>38. More-so, passing a decree in a suit for Specific Performance of Contract is a discretionary relief at the discretion of the Court, to have the such relief the plaintiff must come with clean hand but from the events of the case it is apparent that the plaintiff, the defendant No. 1 and his so called attorney did not make the agreement for sale in clean hand. The plaintiff rather, has created the agreement for purchase of the property who is not in possession of the same and thereafter she played a highly unpleasant events in the name of taking over the possession of the suit property in connivance with her husband which proved that the agreement for sale following transaction as consideration is nothing but a concocted and fabricated events only to grab the property abusing the process of the court in the name of Specific Performance of Contract through an agreement for sale.</u>

39. The pertinent question is whether D.N.A holder can handover the possession of the abandoned property to a party who is none but his wife who make a contract for purchase the property or the D.N.A holder under obligation to handover the possession of the property to the Government ?

40. We are of the considered view that the status of a D.N.A. holder is nothing more then a allottee from the authorise person of the Government not a tenant or representative of original owner. We are therefore of the opinion that such allottee has no locus-standi to handover the possession of a abandoned property to a third party who make a contract to a party claiming the ownership who had/has never in possession of the property. Any D.N.A holder if make any such nature of handing over of possession of a abandoned property it would be surely treated as serious violation of the stipulation of the allotment of D.N.A holder as the D.N.A holder having no right, title or possession as a matter of personal or individual but allottee of the government such handing over of possession must be treated as nonest in the eye of law.

41. The precedences referred by the learned Advocate for the appellant on perusal the same it appear that the facts and circumstances of these cases are quite distinguishable from the facts of the case in hand. Therefore, although we are not disagreeing with those principles, however, we are unable to accept and make those applicable in the present case.

42. Thus, the appeal having no merit, it fails.

43. Accordingly, the appeal is disallowed however, without any order as to cost.

44. Office is directed to communicate the Judgment to the trial Court and send down the lower Court's record at once.

End.

parties:
MD. ABDUS SAMAD 
vs. 
MD. SAMSHER ALI AND OTHERS.
full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J. The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 11.02.2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Rangpur in Miscellaneous Appeal No.24 of 2002 disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 10.02.2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Kawnia, Rangpur in Miscellaneous Case No.12 of 2001 disallowing the case, should not be set aside and/or such other order or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts giving rise to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioner as pre-emptor instituted the original Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No.12 of 2001 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Kawnia, Rangpur under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 against the pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 and others contending inter alia that the ease joie appertaining to Mouza-Raghunathpur under Kawnia police station of District-Rangpur corresponding to S.A. khatian No.34 originally belonged to one Chhutku Mahmud. The S.A. recorded tenant Chhutku Mahmud had been owning and possessing 1.65 acres of land including the case land measuring 0.30 acres. Subsequently, he transferred the total 1.65 acres of land in favour of one Afuruddin. Afuruddin died leaving behind one wife Shahijan Nessa and 04(four) sons namely Abdus Samad, Abdur Hamid, Abdus Salam and Abul Hossain and two daughters namely Afton Nessa and Rashida Khatun. Thereafter, Abdul Hamid transferred .29 acres of land to his brother Md. Abdus Samad by a registered sale deed No.2863 dated 04.05.1987 and on the same date Shahijan Nessa transferred 0.20 1/2 acres of land by a registered heba-bil-awaj deed No.2864 to Abdus Samad and Abdul Hamid. The opposite party No. 2 and 4-7 transferred their respective land in favour of Abdus Samad by different deeds and in this way Abdus Samad become a co-sharer in the case Khatian No.34. The further case of the pre-emptor-petitioner Abdus Samad is such that the opposite party No.2 Abdul Hamid transferred the case land measuring 0.30 acres of land by a registered deed No.3021 on 20.06.2000 in favour of the opposite party No.1 Md. Shamser Ali, a stranger to the case jute, and no notice of transfer was served upon the pre-emptor-petitioner Abdus Samad and to deprive the pre-emptor-petitioner's right to pre-emption, the transfer deed was written in the name and style of an "Exchange Deed," but in fact, the said deed is a sub-kabala deed in favour of stranger opposite party No.1.The pre-emptor-petitioner knowing about the case transfer finally on 14.08.2001 after getting certified copy of the deed, filed the original pre-emption miscellaneous case for getting the case land pre-empted.

3. The contrary case of the purchaser opposite party No.1 in short is thus that the transfer deed is out and out a ‘deed of exchange' and it is not at all a sub-kabala in favour of the pre-emptee-purchaser-opposite party No.1, and that the case land measuring 0.30 acres described in the schedule 'Ka' of the pre-emption miscellaneous petition was exchanged by the opposite party No.2 and the opposite party No.1 in exchange of the land of `Ka' schedule, transferred `kha' schedule land measuring .25 acres by a transfer deed dated 27.06.2000 in favour of opposite party No.2, but the pre-emptor-petitioner out of ill-motive to grab the case land on false allegation instituted the original miscellaneous case, which is liable to be disallowed.

4. The learned trial court during trial of the original case after taking evidences from the sides of the respective parties by its judgment and order dated 10.02.2002 disallowed the pre-emption miscellaneous case.

5. Being aggrieved, the pre-emptor-petitioner filed a Miscellaneous Appeal being No.24 of 2002 in the Court of learned District Judge, Rangpur which was transmitted to the 3rd Court of learned Additional District Judge, Rangpur for hearing and disposal and the learned Additional District Judge by the impugned judgment and order dated 11.02.2004 disallowed the miscellaneous appeal affirming the judgment and order passed by the trial Court.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order, the pre-emptor-appellant-petitioner has preferred this civil revision under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule.

7. During hearing of the Rule, Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahmanz the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioner while Mr. M.G. Mahmud (Shahin), the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite parties.

8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that both the courts below in their observation and findings committed error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in holding the view that the transfer deed is a deed of exchange which is not pre-emptable under the law of pre-emption. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellant court during disposal of the original pre-emption miscellaneous case and its subsequent appeal failed to assess the evidence on records in its true perspective and also failed to appreciate that the transfer deed is a colourable transaction, which is out and out a sale deed in disguise of a deed of exchange. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the courts below on the basis of surmise and conjecture passed the judgment and order which is liable to be set aside.

9. As against the aforesaid submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverted the argument advanced from the side of the learned counsel for the petitioner and submits that, neither the trial court nor the Appellate Court during disposal of the original pre-emption miscellaneous case and its subsequent appeal committed any illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the case deed being a deed of exchange, is not pre-emptable under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the courts below rightly appraising the evidence on records in its true perspective, decided the merit of the original case and its subsequent appeal against the pre-emptor-petitioner and in favour of the pre-emptee-opposite party and there is no illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment and order. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the case deed dated 27.06.2000 is out and out an exchange deed and it is not a colourable transaction in disguise of a deed of, exchange, as alleged from the side of the pre-emptor-petitioner and thereby after proper assessment of evidence on records, the learned appellate court disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and order passed by the trial court and there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, by which the impugned   judgment and order can be interfered with.

10. In order to appreciate the submission advanced from the sides of the learned counsels for the parties, having gone through the impugned judgment and order dated 11.02.2004 and the judgment and order passed by the trial court dated 10.02.2002 in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No.12 of 2001 and the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties, both oral and documentary, it transpires that, admittedly the pre-emptor-petitioner is a co-sharer in the case joie and it appears from the pleadings of the parties that, the pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 in his written objection clearly asserted that he did not purchase the case land measuring 0.30 acres of land by way of a sale deed and for the case land, there has been a `deed of exchange'. The opposite party No.2 by a registered deed of exchange dated 27.06.2000 transferred 0.30 acres of land described in schedule 'Ka' in favour of the opposite party No.1 and in exchange of this land, the opposite party No.1 transferred 0.25 acres of land described in schedule `Kha' of the pre-emption miscellaneous petition, in favour of the opposite party No.2. The two deeds have been produced from the side of the pre-emptor-petitioner and have been marked as Exhibit-2 and 3 respectively.

11. Scrutinizing the above mentioned two deeds, it is evident to note that the case deed as it appears in its face is a 'deed of exchange' not sub-kabala and it is the positive contention in the pleadings of the opposite party No.1 and 2 that the case land was not sold in favour of the opposite party No.1 by the opposite party No.2, rather; it was exchanged pursuant to deed No.3021/2000 and 3398/2001.

12. Both the parties to the case to substantiate their respective pleading's case have adduced witnesses.

13. P.W.1 is the pre-emptor-petitioner Md. Abdus Samad. This witness in his testimony testified in his examination-in-chief that, 0.30 acres of land has been transferred by the opposite party No.2 in favour of opposite party No.1 on 13th instant of 2000 A.D. Subsequently, the pre-emptor as P.W.1 testifies that on 13th Ashar, 1407 B.S. the transfer was held. During cross-examination P.W.1 testified at a stage that the case land is 0.30 acres and the consideration amount was shown in the deed as Tk.3000/- (three thousand) only. In a reply to a question from the side of the opposite party, P.W.1 testified that in the concerned area, the price of land is Tk.300/-(three hundred) per decimal. P.W.1 denied that inasmuch as, it was a deed of exchange, the value shown against the deed is not the actual value.

14. P.W.2 Abul Kalam Azad in his testimony testified that he knows the parties and the case land was transferred by Abdul Hamid in favour of Shamsher Ali. During cross-examination P.W.2 testified at a stage that, he is the paternal brother of the pre-emptor-petitioner and he was not present at the time of registration of the deed and he is also not a witness to the deed.

15. Vis-à-vis; O.P.W.1 Shamsher Ali in his testimony testified that he has exchanged some land with the opposite party No.2 and the case deed is a deed of exchange not a sub-kabala. O.P.W.1 denied that to frustrate the right of pre-emption, they have created the transfer deed as a deed of exchange. During cross-examination from the side of the pre-emptor, O.P.W.1 testified at a stage that in their locality the actual price of the land is Tk.1,000/-(one thousand) per decimal. O.P.W.2 Abdul Hamid testified before the court that he is the opposite party No.2 and full brother of the pre-emptor-petitioner. O.P.W.2 further testified that he has exchanged the case land with Shamsher Ali and the deed was executed and registered as a deed of exchange.

16. O.P.W.3 Md. Nafar Uddin testified that he knows the parties and the case land and the case land described in schedule 'Ka' has been exchanged with the land described in schedule `Kha' and the exchange was done between Abdul Hamid and Shamsher Ali. O.P.W.3 further testified that on the date of registration of the deed, he went to the Sub-registry office. During cross-examination O.P.W.3 further testified that on the date of registration, Shamsher Ali called him to accompany.

<u>17. Analyzing the case records and the evidences from the sides of the respective parties, I have the reason to draw such inference that practically in the concerned locality, the actual price of the land as cited by the pre-emptor in his testimony, was Tk.1,000/(one thousand) per decimal at the relevant time, but it appears from the deed-in-question that 30 decimals of land was transferred in lieu of Tk.3,000/-(three thousand) only. The courts below in their observation and findings concurrently held that inasmuch as, it was not a sale deed, for exchanging the land between O.P.W.1 and O.P.W.2, the value of the land was shown inadequate which is a strong circumstantial evidence in this case. Besides this, having gone through the testimonies of the witnesses it is evident to note that P.W.1 and P.W.2 in their examination-in-chief, despite tried to corroborate the pleadings case of the pre-emptor-petitioner, but both of them have been discredited in their cross-examination and on the other hand, O.P,Ws. 1-3 corroborated one-another in respect of the pleading's case of the opposite party. Except some minor discrepancies no such material contradiction or omission is noticed, by dint of which these witnesses can be disbelieved.</u>

<u>18. Under the ambit of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 [XXVIII of 1951]. it is a decided matter in our judicature that in case of a colourable transaction, the onus of proof is entirely lies upon the party, who assert that the transfer is a sub-kabala in disguise of a deed of exchange under section 101 and 103 of the Evidence Act [I of 1872]. Apart from this, the contents of the deed will get priority until and unless it is rebutted by sufficient convincing credible evidence, with that of the oral evidence adduced from the sides of the parties. It is the incumbent duty upon the pre-emptor-petitioner to prove by sufficient tangible, credible evidence that the deed-in-question is out and out a sale deed, in disguise of a deed of exchange.</u>

19. In the instant case, I have come across from the evidence on records that the pre-emptor-petitioner has failed to discharge his onus of proof and the courts below concurrently in their observation and findings on the basis of evidences on records, rightly held that the deed-in-question is purely a deed of exchange, not a sub-kabala and as such it is not pre-emptable under the ambit of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950.

20. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and the discussions referred to above, I am constrained to hold such a view that in the impugned judgment and order there is no illegality or infirmity or misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, by which it can be interfered with.

21. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The impugned judgment and order dated 11.02.2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Rangpur in Miscellaneous Appeal No.24 of 2002 disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 10.02.2002 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Kawnia, Rangpur in Miscellaneous Case No.12 of 2001 is hereby affirmed.

22. However, there will be no order as to costs.

23. Communicate the judgment and order at once and send back to the Lower Court's Records immediately.

End.
